name: Reconcile Cluster
description: Top-level Reconcile loop: validates the spec and the image tag against the version the servers run (status.version) on every pass, refusing with phase Failed and a ValidationFailed event, provisions TLS/RBAC/Services/ConfigMap, applies the server StatefulSet (holding replicas during a scale-down drain, and keeping the partition a Paused or Failed upgrade left, also when a storage expansion creates the StatefulSet again), collects diagnostics once the cluster has formed, and marks the cluster Ready once formation and rollout are both verified (announcing ClusterReady only when that write takes the cluster into Ready from another phase, never when it only moves the message, a condition or the generation of a cluster already Ready; #606, operations.md id 136) (the servers a held upgrade keeps below its partition are not a rollout in flight, and status.message then names the held upgrade, operations.md id 149) (recording status.version from the rolled server StatefulSet when it differs: at the first Ready, and after an image the zero-ready escape hatch let through, but not while a Failed or Paused upgrade targets that tag — operations.md id 144), requeueing a Ready cluster after --ready-poll-interval (default 30s; every other path keeps RequeueAfter) — or hands a cluster that is short of servers to the shortfall assessment. On deletion, it deletes the {name}-tls-secret cert-manager issued for its {name}-tls Certificate (#479), and releasing the finalizer withdraws the cluster's metric series. The server pods run under the {cluster}-discovery ServiceAccount, bound to no Role (LIST discovery never calls the Kubernetes API); a {cluster}-discovery Role, RoleBinding or Service (V1 port 5000) the cluster controls, created by releases up to v1.20, is deleted. A failed pass is retried on its own 5–30s backoff, with a shared 10/s storm guard. ApplyDefaults' defaults go on the pass's own copy and are never written back: the finalizer is added and released, and the scale-down and Aura fleet deployment annotations are set, as merge patches of what changed (with the object's resourceVersion), never as an Update, which wrote the defaults, a false the CRD defaults to true as true, and a quantity in its canonical spelling into the stored spec. The stored spec stays the one the user applied (operations.md id 150). A template write the StatefulSet controller has not observed (observedGeneration behind generation), or a cached read older than the generation the pass wrote, is a rollout in flight, so the pass does not report a stale Ready from its own write; status.observedGeneration and the conditions' observedGeneration are the generation the pass read and acted on. The Ready pass records, with the Ready status and only when they change, the versions the servers report for a tag without a patch (status.runningVersion; for a held upgrade status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion), read from the formation check's SHOW SERVERS (operations.md id 153). A refused spec (validation, server role hints, property sharding, a missing StorageClass) is logged at info on the pass that announces it and at V(1) on the passes in between, never as an ERROR on every pass (operations.md id 136). Every label that carries the image tag (app.kubernetes.io/version) carries it without a digest, cut to a valid label value, so a tag pinned to a digest no longer fails the ConfigMap write (#562 walk; id 149). A server StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again as it was (Recreate StatefulSet As It Was, id 171). A deletion whose finalizer release finds the cluster already gone is done, logged at V(1), not an ERROR and a reconcile error (operations.md id 164). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). After the StatefulSet apply it replaces a server pod that cannot start and is due for the update, where the StatefulSet controller does not (MaxUnavailableStatefulSet in Kubernetes 1.35.0–1.35.3); the server StatefulSet says maxUnavailable 1, outside the pod template, so writing it restarts nothing (operations.md id 204). A shared-list variable of the cluster's spec.env is rendered into neo4j.conf, not onto the server StatefulSet; the template write that stops owning such a variable hands it to the plugins that have written to the StatefulSet (handOverSharedLists: the value their list settings ask for, or dropped when none), so moving it rolls the servers once and the plugins write nothing (operations.md id 209).

name: Reconcile Cluster ConfigMap
description: Renders the cluster's {cluster}-config ConfigMap (neo4j.conf, startup.sh, health.sh) and decides whether the servers must restart. The restart decision compares a normalised rendering that drops full-line comments and blank lines and masks runtime-variable lines. When only neo4j.conf changed and every changed setting is dynamic (SHOW SETTINGS isDynamic), not set by an env var, and the cluster is Ready with every server up, it runs dbms.setConfigValue on every server first and restarts nothing (ConfigAppliedLive); otherwise it stamps config-restart on the server StatefulSet, rolling every server (ConfigNeedsRestart says why). The ConfigMap is written whenever its raw content changes, after any live apply, so a later restart keeps the values. Startup-script lines between the restart-neutral markers (the system database role block, which makes servers past minSystemPrimaries system secondaries at their first start and records the role on their volume; the procedure-list block) never count; the procedure-list block (buildPluginListMergeBlock) gives each shared procedure and extension list a Neo4jPlugin sets as a NEO4J_<setting> variable the entries neo4j.conf holds for it too — the cluster's spec.config list and the fleetManagement.* entry of spec.auraFleetManagement — before the Neo4j entrypoint, which writes such a variable in place of the conf's line, so a plugin's list adds to the cluster's own instead of replacing it (the union, the conf's tokens first, each once), and an allowlist set anywhere gets fleetManagement.* while NEO4J_PLUGINS lists fleet-management; an operator upgrade that adds it restarts nothing, and a server gets the union at its next start (operations.md id 179); a change confined to the membership lines (TOTAL_SERVERS, the discovery endpoint list) restarts nothing unless a scale-up adds a system primary (ScaledWithoutRestart). It records on the ConfigMap which settings it applies at the next restart and since when (neo4j.com/deferred-settings, neo4j.com/deferred-settings-since). When spec.monitoring.logs.stdout lists a log, it also renders server-logs.xml (Neo4j's default file appenders for the line plus a JSON Console appender per listed log) and adds server.logs.config=/operator-conf/server-logs.xml; the restart hash never covers server-logs.xml, so a changed list reloads through the mount without a restart. neo4j.conf sets dbms.cluster.network.connect_timeout=5s (Neo4j's default is 30s) unless spec.config sets it: a replaced pod's old IP can stay in the other servers' DNS cache for up to 30s, and a connection to it waits out the whole timeout. health.sh never counts for the restart decision: the probes run the copy each container makes at its start, so a new version reaches every server at its next restart and an operator upgrade restarts nothing for it (knowledge operations.md id 181). With spec.auraFleetManagement, neo4j.conf always puts fleetManagement.* in dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted and in dbms.security.procedures.allowlist only when the cluster's own spec.config sets the allowlist, as the Operations Manual asks for a plugin; an allowlist of fleetManagement.* alone loaded nothing else (operations.md id 192). The Neo4j image's entrypoint itself adds dbms.security.procedures.allowlist=fleetManagement.* for fleet-management in NEO4J_PLUGINS to a neo4j.conf without the setting (apply_plugin_default_configuration); the list block exports the variable as Neo4j's default, *, when nothing sets the allowlist, and the entrypoint's environment pass, which runs after, puts it in place of that line (id 192). The entrypoint likewise adds each installed plugin's own dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted entry (apoc.*, gds.*, bloom.*, genai.* — genai.*,ai.* from 2026.10.0 — fleetManagement.*) only to a neo4j.conf without that list, and a variable replaces it; so, unless the cluster sets the unrestricted list itself (its spec.config, or NEO4J_dbms_security_procedures_unrestricted in its spec.env: an explicit setting wins, OwnsUnrestrictedList), the block (operator_plugin_defaults, the plugin-defaults argument of operator_merge_list) reads those entries from the image's own /startup/neo4j-plugins.json with jq and adds them to an unrestricted list the conf or the variable sets; restart-neutral like the rest of the block, so each server gets them at its next start (operations.md id 193). neo4j.conf also holds the shared procedure and extension lists the cluster's spec.env sets as NEO4J_<setting> variables with a value of their own, unioned with its spec.config list; they are left off the StatefulSet, so that variable is the plugins' and the startup block joins the two (operations.md id 209). The startup script puts the Neo4j image's own server.jvm.additional lines, less -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch (which pre-touched the whole heap and got a server at the documented minimum OOMKilled under write load), first in /conf/neo4j.conf, read from the image's neo4j.conf before the entrypoint replaces that directory, in a restart-neutral block: NEO4J_server_jvm_additional follows them and wins a conflicting flag — the operator's list, then the cluster's own server.jvm.additional (spec.config's, then a plain spec.env value), which adds to the list and no longer replaces it; spec.config's line is left out of neo4j.conf (only a spec.env value from a Secret or ConfigMap keeps the old shape: the user's variable, no operator list, the conf line kept) — and the operator upgrade that adds the block restarts no server (operations.md ids 208, 212). The restart decision compares the desired ConfigMap with the existing one less its server.jvm.additional lines when the desired neo4j.conf has none (withoutMovedJVMLines): the line leaving the conf is not a roll of its own, the variable's change on the pod template is the cluster's one roll at the upgrade (id 208). When the cluster's spec no longer installs Aura Fleet Management, the restart stamp also takes the fleet-management entry Fleet Management recorded out of NEO4J_PLUGINS, in the same StatefulSet write, so the disable rolls the servers once (sf-remove-fleet-plugin, operations.md id 222). The same write carries the cluster's own NEO4J_PLUGINS (its spec.env sets it) as the cluster renders it now, so turning Fleet Management on or off on such a cluster rolls the servers once (carryOwnNeo4jPlugins, sf-own-plugins-fleet-entry, operations.md id 223). While spec.auraFleetManagement installs the plugin, its restart stamp also adds fleet-management to a NEO4J_PLUGINS the cluster does not own, recorded as Fleet Management's, so an enable is one roll (addFleetEntryInWrite; operations.md id 226).

name: Cluster Server Readiness Check
description: buildHealthScript renders /conf/health.sh, which the readiness, liveness and startup probes of every cluster server run. Until the server has been seen available in this container, and for at most ReadyWindowSeconds (300) of the container's age, it passes only when the server is available in the cluster as it sees itself: GET /db/system/cluster/available answers 200 and GET /dbms/cluster/status reports no unhealthy database and no primary out of its Raft group, read on the local HTTP port with the container's admin credentials through bash's /dev/tcp. Afterwards, and when the container's age cannot be read, it checks the process and the HTTP port only, so the liveness probe never restarts a server for being out of the cluster. A StatefulSet roll (plugin, config, TLS) therefore restarts the next server only after the previous one rejoined; first formation is not held back (Parallel pod management, not-ready addresses published). The probes are unchanged, so no pod template moves (knowledge operations.md ids 6, 181).

name: Reconcile RestartPending
description: Maintains the RestartPending condition for settings the operator applies at each server's next restart instead of restarting for them. Two kinds: startup-script settings written by the restart-neutral block (dbms.cluster.raft.async_channel_acquisition_enabled on 5.26.29+, dbms.security.tls_reload_enabled on CalVer 2025.03+ with cert-manager TLS), and live changes of restart-effective dynamic settings that a live apply changes only in part (dbms.cluster.network.connect_timeout: Raft connections take it up only at a restart). The two have separate records on the cluster ConfigMap: neo4j.com/deferred-settings(-since) for the startup-script settings, and neo4j.com/restart-effective-settings(-since), stamped by ReconcileConfigMap only when a write changes such a setting's value against the running ConfigMap (an added line on upgrade from v1.20.x, or a spec.config edit; an unchanged value or a new ConfigMap records nothing). A server is waiting for a setting when its Neo4j has it (dbms.components() per pod, only for a version-gated setting) and its neo4j container started before that setting's record. With neither record the condition is absent. SHOW SETTINGS is not used: on 5.26.31 it misreports the async Raft setting, and it reports a live-applied value the Raft connections do not use yet. Best-effort; re-reads only when the pods or the settings change. Its per-server connection (dialClusterPod, shared with live config changes and TLS reloads) reads the admin Secret the servers were given, spec.auth.adminSecret or the default neo4j-admin-secret when it is unset; it used to refuse a cluster without the field (operations.md id 132).

name: Reload Renewed TLS Certificate
description: When {name}-tls-secret (owned by cert-manager, watched by name) holds a certificate the servers do not present, reads dbms.security.tls_reload_enabled on each ready server and, where it is true, runs dbms.security.reloadTLS() and confirms the certificate a new TLS connection gets (the procedure also succeeds, doing nothing, when reload is disabled). Retries while the kubelet projects the files (throttled to 30s, up to 10 minutes after the certificate's NotBefore), reports servers that must restart instead, and records the fingerprint on the StatefulSet (neo4j.com/tls-certificate). Shared by the cluster and standalone reconcilers; CalVer 2025.03+ with cert-manager TLS only.

name: Reconcile OpenShift Route
description: Creates or updates the OpenShift Route of a cluster or standalone (spec.service.route: {name}-client-route or {name}-route) and of its MCP server ({name}-mcp-route), shared by both reconcilers (reconcileRoute, reconcileMCPRoute). The mutate step (applyDesiredRoute) writes what the operator renders — labels, annotations, spec.to, spec.port, spec.path, spec.host when the user names one, and spec.tls termination and insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy — and keeps the rest: the wildcardPolicy and generated host (with its openshift.io/host.generated annotation) OpenShift's API server fills in, and a certificate added to the Route by hand, so a Route that is already right is not written again (#536). tls.secretName is not rendered and raises a ValidationWarning. Without the Route API it skips the Route and raises an advisory RouteAPINotFound (knowledge operations.md ids 102, 145, 148).

name: Merge Fleet Management Plugin
description: Phase 1 of Aura Fleet Management, for a cluster or standalone with spec.auraFleetManagement.enabled: addFleetManagementPlugin merges fleet-management into the neo4j container's NEO4J_PLUGINS with MergeNeo4jPluginList. It runs in the write that creates the StatefulSet — after the record of the env the deployment owns, so NEO4J_PLUGINS stays out of the static template and out of that record — so a new deployment's servers start with the plugin; and on every pass as mergeFleetManagementPlugin, which writes only when the entry is missing. Enabling it on a running deployment restarts the servers once: the enable's neo4j.conf change rolls them, and that roll's write carries the name, recorded as Fleet Management's — a cluster's ConfigMap restart stamp (triggerRollingRestartForConfigChange calls addFleetEntryInWrite), a standalone's StatefulSet write with its new conf hash. The cluster's merge decides from the cached StatefulSet, waits while a conf roll is due (confRollPending) and writes against a read from the API server, so a cache that has not seen the stamp writes nothing; the standalone's merge waits while the conf its StatefulSet records is not the one it renders (standaloneConfRollDue). It was two controllerrevisions in the same second on a cluster, the stamp then the merge (#608; operations.md id 226). A StatefulSet that does not exist yet is not a failure; anything else raises AuraFleetManagementPluginPatchFailed (knowledge operations.md ids 164, 175). A failure that lasts is announced once per cause (fleetPluginPatchFailures, operations.md id 145), and logged at info when announced, at V(1) on the passes in between, never as an ERROR or a reconcile error (id 164); an image whose entrypoint does not list fleet-management never gets here — the validator refuses the spec (id 191). Its procedures go in the unrestricted list always and in the allowlist only beside an allowlist something else sets (operations.md id 192). Not on an image with Fleet Manager built in (CalVer 2026.03 and later, validation.FleetManagementBuiltIn on the template's image): the image's entrypoint cannot install the plugin there (no JAR in products/, no versions URL: it wgets "null" and starts without it) and the procedures are the server's own; the merge never removes an entry an earlier write made while Fleet Management is enabled, so nothing restarts (operations.md id 192); turning it off takes a recorded entry out (sf-remove-fleet-plugin). Its write is marked (fleetPluginWriteError), so AuraFleetManagementPluginPatchFailed says "Failed to add" only when the write failed, and names the check otherwise; the merge still runs on a built-in image, judged by the template's own neo4j container (operations.md id 192). The write that adds the name records it as Fleet Management's, in the same write, under the StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/aura-fleet-management-entries (not when the deployment's own spec.env sets NEO4J_PLUGINS); the pass keeps that record in line with a patch of the StatefulSet's metadata that restarts nothing, made against a read from the API server — on a cluster after its template apply (reconcileFleetEntry), on a standalone in the merge, which runs after its StatefulSet write: it adopts an entry an earlier operator added, or one the merge keeps on 2026.03+, when no Neo4jPlugin claims the name, and drops a record whose entry is gone (keepFleetRecord, operations.md id 222). It never writes a NEO4J_PLUGINS the deployment owns (its spec.env sets it, and its record of its env lists it): the cluster's template apply put its own value back over the merge's and the servers restarted without end (#608); the deployment carries the name in that list itself (sf-own-plugins-fleet-entry, operations.md id 223). A NEO4J_PLUGINS read from a Secret or ConfigMap is never written (a value beside valueFrom is refused by the API server), and a value that is not a JSON list does not fail the deployment's own write (errNeo4jPluginsNotAList). Plugin-only mode (neither tokenSecretRef nor provision) is logged at info once, at V(1) on the passes after, and again once it comes back after a token source, a disable or a deletion ended it (logFleetRegistrationDeferred; operations.md id 145).

name: Take Out Fleet Management's Plugin Entry
description: When a cluster's or standalone's spec no longer installs Aura Fleet Management (spec.auraFleetManagement.enabled false, or the block removed), the fleet-management entry its own path recorded (StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/aura-fleet-management-entries) leaves the neo4j container's NEO4J_PLUGINS and the record goes. An entry a Neo4jPlugin claims — its neo4j.com/plugin-entries.<plugin> record lists it, or an enabled, Managed plugin of the target adds it as its name or a dependency — or a NEO4J_PLUGINS the deployment's own spec.env sets stays, and only the record goes; an entry nothing recorded (a deployment whose Fleet Management was already off when the operator was upgraded) stays, for a by-hand removal. The disable also changes neo4j.conf, which rolls the servers, and the removal rides that roll's write: a cluster's ConfigMap restart stamp (triggerRollingRestartForConfigChange), a standalone's StatefulSet write carrying its new conf hash, only when that hash is the conf the standalone renders now (standaloneFleetEntryDue). A removal no conf change carries is written alone: by the standalone's same StatefulSet write, and on a cluster by removeFleetManagementPlugin after the template apply (reconcileFleetEntry) while no conf roll is due (confRollPending), reading the StatefulSet from the API server first. It waits for nothing a plugin waits for (it is the deployment's own spec change) and is never written into the first step of a two-step recreate (operations.md id 222). A NEO4J_PLUGINS the deployment's own spec.env sets has no record: it goes back to the user's list in the same roll, a cluster's through the restart stamp carrying the list as the cluster renders it (sf-own-plugins-fleet-entry, operations.md id 223).

name: Carry Fleet Management's Entry in the Deployment's Own NEO4J_PLUGINS
description: A NEO4J_PLUGINS the deployment's own spec.env sets is the deployment's (operations.md id 223). While spec.auraFleetManagement installs the plugin on an image whose entrypoint installs it (not FleetManagementBuiltIn, 2026.03+), the cluster renders fleet-management into its own list (clusterNeo4jPlugins, MergeNeo4jPluginList: the user's names and order kept, a list that names it already byte for byte) in the server StatefulSet it builds for the normal pass and the upgrade's Staging (buildServerStatefulSet), so its template hash and owned-env record take that value, its template apply puts it back like any of its variables, and the fleet merge finds the name and writes nothing. Turning Fleet Management on or off changes neo4j.conf and the list together: the ConfigMap's restart stamp carries the list as the cluster renders it (carryOwnNeo4jPlugins), so each toggle is one roll; off, the list is what the user wrote, and a fleet-management the user wrote stays. The template apply that stops owning the variable keeps fleet-management in it, recorded as Fleet Management's, in the same write (addFleetEntryInWrite). A standalone's template write appends the name to its own list (its controller never puts a live value back, so it never looped), in the write its conf hash moves on the same toggle. A list read from a Secret or ConfigMap, or not a JSON list, is left as the spec gives it, with the validator's ValidationWarning. A Neo4jPlugin is still refused such a variable (operations.md id 135). A variable the deployment owns carries no record: when spec.env sets NEO4J_PLUGINS again while Fleet Management is on, the template write that takes it back drops neo4j.com/aura-fleet-management-entries in that write (addFleetEntryInWrite), and the enabled pass's upkeep drops a record a build before left with a metadata patch (fleetRecordUpkeep; operations.md id 227).

name: Provision Aura Fleet Manager deployment and token
description: Phase 0 of Aura Fleet Management for a cluster or standalone with spec.auraFleetManagement.provision (reconcileAuraFleetProvision in aura_fleet_provision.go, shared by both reconcilers): resolves the Aura credentials, organization and project; ensures a Fleet Manager deployment — the neo4j.com/external-fleet-deployment-id annotation, else one of the same name (adopted), else CreateDeployment, the annotation written before any token is minted; then ensures the token Secret — POST mints a first token, and when one already exists the token is rotated only if never registered or under tokenPolicy: Rotate, else refused with an explanation. Non-fatal: every failure is a status.auraFleetManagement.message, never a reconcile error. Only an Aura call marked retryable at the call (retryableAuraCall) is retried quietly; a Kubernetes write that fails (the annotation, the token Secret) is reported. Messages leave Aura's request ID out (knowledge operations.md ids 86, 88, 184).

name: Deprovision Aura Fleet Manager deployment
description: deprovisionAuraFleet, from the cluster's or standalone's deletion: when the provision block says deletionPolicy: Delete and managementPolicies permit Delete, revokes the deployment's token, then unregisters the deployment recorded in the annotation. Best-effort and non-fatal: a stuck Aura API never holds the finalizer.

name: Reconcile Standalone
description: Top-level standalone reconcile: validates the spec on every pass with StandaloneValidator.Validate (the spec rules, the admin-secret password shape, and spec.image.tag against status.version: a downgrade turns it Failed with a ValidationFailed event and leaves the pod on the version it runs), reconciles TLS/ConfigMap/Service/StatefulSet/Ingress, runs a pre-upgrade health check and announces UpgradeStarted on the pass that applies a new image (the StatefulSet's template does not carry it yet), and updates status once the StatefulSet reports one ready replica. status.version is the image tag of a StatefulSet whose pod is ready on the current template, never spec.image.tag. Both upgrade strategies give the StatefulSet RollingUpdate, which replaces the one pod; Recreate used to select OnDelete, under which a new image, config or plugin never reached the server (operations.md id 144). A Ready standalone requeues after --ready-poll-interval (default 30s); otherwise RequeueAfter. With spec.podServiceAccountAnnotations it creates the `<name>-neo4j` ServiceAccount before the StatefulSet and runs the pod under it, and deletes it once the field is removed and no pod uses it. The pod template carries a hash of the raw neo4j.conf, so a changed conf restarts the pod; a change only in comments or blank lines keeps the running pod's hash (the normalised conf hash is recorded on the StatefulSet) and restarts nothing. A neo4j.conf change of dynamic settings only is applied to the running pod with dbms.setConfigValue before the conf is written, and the pod keeps its hash. With cert-manager TLS on CalVer 2025.03+, its conf enables TLS reload (applied at the next restart, ignored by the restart decision) and a renewed certificate is reloaded on the running pod. On deletion it deletes the {name}-tls-secret cert-manager issued for its {name}-tls-cert Certificate (#479). With spec.monitoring.logs.stdout it writes server-logs.xml into its ConfigMap (deleting it when no log is listed) and points server.logs.config at /conf/server-logs.xml, so Neo4j's listed logs reach standard output as JSON. The finalizer is added and released, and the Aura fleet deployment annotation set, as merge patches of what changed, never as an Update, which wrote the spec back as the Go types encode it (an explicit monitoring.enabled: false came back true); the stored spec stays the one the user applied (operations.md id 150). For a status.version without a patch it records status.runningVersion, the version the server reports, with one SHOW SERVERS once Ready and again only when its container runs another image; updateStatus clears it when status.version moves (operations.md id 153). Its OpenShift Route is written once per pass at most, at the end of the Service step (a second, unconditional write later in the pass was removed, #536). status.observedGeneration and the Ready condition's are the generation the pass acted on, not the one its write re-reads (#550; operations.md id 153). Its status is Ready only when its pod is ready on the StatefulSet's latest pod template; while a template write rolls out it is Pending ("Waiting for the standalone to restart on its latest pod template: …"). A refused spec or a missing StorageClass is logged at info on the pass that announces it and at V(1) after, never as an ERROR on every pass (operations.md id 136). A StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again as it was, so its pod is not replaced (id 171). A deletion whose finalizer release finds the standalone already gone is done, logged at V(1) (operations.md id 164). A StatefulSet a storage expansion deleted is created again in the same pass once the delete has gone through. Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its UpgradeStarted belongs to the pass that writes the new image, read from the API server rather than the cache, so a stale read does not announce it twice (#565; operations.md id 144). Its neo4j.conf is rendered by desiredStandaloneConfigMap (standalone_conf.go), which the plugin controller's allowlist check shares (operations.md id 194), with the keys someone else put in the live ConfigMap merged back by mergeStandaloneConf. Aura Fleet Management's allowlist entry, and a fleet-management Neo4jPlugin's automatic one, join the standalone's neo4j.conf allowlist only when its own spec.config, its spec.env or another plugin sets it; fleetManagement.* always goes in the unrestricted list (collectStandalonePluginConf, renderStandaloneConfigMap; operations.md id 192). A procedure or extension list its spec.env sets as a NEO4J_<setting> variable, not read from a Secret or ConfigMap, is joined into its neo4j.conf and left off its StatefulSet (resources.SpecEnvLists, shared with the cluster, id 209), since the entrypoint wrote it in place of the conf's line; one from a Secret or ConfigMap stays a variable (id 193). An unrestricted list its conf sets and the standalone does not set itself (its spec.config or its spec.env) gets the image's entry for each plugin its NEO4J_PLUGINS installs (ImageUnrestrictedDefaults; id 193), one restart where that changes the conf. With fleet-management in NEO4J_PLUGINS on an image that installs it (before 2026.03) and no allowlist set anywhere, its neo4j.conf carries dbms.security.procedures.allowlist=*, so the image's entrypoint does not narrow it to fleetManagement.* (id 192). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). The standalone's neo4j.conf opens with the Neo4j image's own server.jvm.additional lines, less -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch, from a per-release table (a newer CalVer gets the newest known list), between restart-neutral markers that its restart decision leaves out (withoutDeferredConf): the operator upgrade that adds them restarts no standalone, and the user's lines and the truststore flags follow and win a conflicting flag (operations.md id 212).

name: Merge Env Vars
description: Computes the StatefulSet container's next env-var list: applies the cluster controller's desired vars, drops names in the previously-owned annotation that are no longer desired, and preserves foreign vars added by plugin/fleet/Aura controllers.

name: Merge Init Containers and Volumes
description: On a template apply of the server StatefulSet, merges the pod template's init containers and volumes by name (mergeOwnedByName): applies what the cluster renders, drops what it rendered on its last apply (recorded in the neo4j.com/cluster-controller-init-containers and neo4j.com/cluster-controller-volumes StatefulSet annotations, written from the desired template) and no longer renders, and keeps the rest — a VerifiedDownload Neo4jPlugin's init container and its plugin-auth/plugin-ca volumes. The comparisons that decide whether a stable cluster's template changed leave those kept items out, so they never trigger an apply. A StatefulSet without the record (an earlier operator's) counts every init container as the cluster's except those listed in the plugin controller's neo4j.com/plugin-init-containers pod-template annotation, and every volume except those only such an init container mounts.

name: Collect Cluster Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW SERVERS and SHOW DATABASES against a cluster that has formed — Ready, Degraded, or mid-rollout with ClusterFormed=True, so it keeps reporting while a server is down —, fills the address of a server that is down from the per-cluster address book (SHOW SERVERS reports none for it), and writes results plus ServersHealthy/DatabasesHealthy conditions into status.diagnostics; non-fatal — every error is surfaced only in status.diagnostics.collectionError, never returned to the caller. The result is written to status only when it changed (lists sorted; databases' transaction counters ignored) or lastCollected is 5 minutes old: a status write re-enqueues the reconcile, so writing every pass looped it (#475). A query that fails because a server could not be reached (a pod deleted or restarting, ConnectivityError: EOF) is logged at info; any other failure is logged as an error (#549; knowledge operations.md id 164). Neo4j answering "not now" — a Neo.TransientError.* (a database unavailable while it restarts or fails over), NotALeader — is logged at info like a server that cannot be reached (IsTransientError); a real error stays at error (knowledge operations.md id 164). During an active upgrade the same SHOW SERVERS also writes the Degraded condition — True (ServersUnavailable) naming each Enabled server that is not Available, False once every server is — and nothing else: the phase stays as the upgrade keeps it and no step gate reads the condition; with spec.monitoring.enabled false that SHOW SERVERS still runs. A Rolling step with server-2 in ImagePullBackOff for 30 minutes read Degraded=False before (#594; operations.md id 214).

name: Collect Standalone Diagnostics
description: Runs SHOW DATABASES (plus users/roles) against a Ready standalone instance and writes status.diagnostics; non-fatal, mirroring the cluster path's collectionError-only error handling. The result is written to status only when it changed (lists sorted; databases' transaction counters ignored) or lastCollected is 5 minutes old: a status write re-enqueues the reconcile, so writing every pass looped it (#475). A query that fails because the server could not be reached is logged at info; any other failure as an error (#549). Neo4j answering "not now" — a Neo.TransientError.* (a database unavailable while it restarts or fails over), NotALeader — is logged at info like a server that cannot be reached (IsTransientError); a real error stays at error (knowledge operations.md id 164).

name: Collect Users And Roles
description: Runs SHOW USERS and SHOW ROLES, sorts and caps each result list at 50 rows, and appends any query failure to the shared collectionError string without aborting the rest of diagnostics collection (e.g. when the connecting user lacks SHOW USER/SHOW ROLE privilege).

name: Advance Rolling Upgrade
description: Dispatches exactly one non-blocking state-machine step per reconcile (Staging, Rolling, Stabilizing, Verifying) and re-stages from any active phase if the target image tag changes mid-flight (a new target below status.version, or below the current target once a server runs it, is refused by the validation that runs before it), so an in-flight upgrade never blocks reconciliation of other clusters. Each phase transition restarts status.upgradeStatus.phaseStartTime and records the ended phase's duration in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds exactly once, derived from the persisted phaseStartTime. In Rolling it lowers the partition only after the server it just restarted is Available and every database copy on it has caught up (statusCheck APPLYING, SHOW DATABASES at requested status), naming the lagging databases in status.upgradeStatus.message (#488). The availability check reads the restarted server's SHOW SERVERS row, version included: for a target without a patch it records that version in status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion once the server is available (operations.md id 153). Completed writes status.version (the tag) with status.runningVersion, the highest version the servers reported to Verifying for a tag without a patch, cleared for one that names its patch. After each step, the pass collects the cluster's diagnostics (SHOW SERVERS, SHOW DATABASES → status.diagnostics, ServersHealthy, DatabasesHealthy, server_health) at most once per --ready-poll-interval, so they follow the servers through the upgrade; nothing else of the normal pass runs while an upgrade is active. Before an upgrade starts it checks the upgrade path with the same rule the validation runs (ValidateVersionUpgrade against status.version). Every image change on a Ready cluster goes through it, whatever spec.upgradeStrategy.strategy says: Recreate is accepted with a ValidationWarning and does what RollingUpgrade does (it used to return before the machine started, so a Ready cluster kept its old image and no other spec change was applied while the tag differed), and the server StatefulSet is always RollingUpdate, never OnDelete. A step's timeout is a Go duration above zero; one at or below zero is refused by validation, and the getters fall back to the default (operations.md id 144). A Paused or Failed upgrade taken up again keeps its start time and progress (operations.md id 149). An upgrade a scale-down drain holds back is announced (UpgradeDeferred) once per target, not on each 15s check (#527). Staging keeps the StatefulSet's replica count, whatever spec.topology.servers says, and freezes the partition at the lowest of the restarted servers that cannot start on the image they run, when the new template changes it, so the StatefulSet replaces them first (operations.md ids 162, 163). Rolling reports a topology change in either direction in the TopologyChangeDeferred condition. Starting, resuming or retargeting an upgrade on a cluster that is Ready with every server available writes its status.message: the upgrade is in progress (#553). Every Rolling pass, a retarget and a resumed held upgrade first record whether a restarted server's neo4j container has started on the target (status.upgradeStatus.startedTargetVersion); a retarget below what a server started on waits, re-checked against that record before it re-stages, since validation may have read it before the server started. On a formed cluster short of servers (the repair walk: Ready with Degraded, Degraded, or Forming) the walk's status.message says the upgrade is in progress and that the servers that could not start are replaced first, keeping the phase, instead of naming the server that was down when it began (#562 walk; operations.md id 149). Staging runs once per target: it reads the stored upgrade record and the StatefulSet uncached and does nothing when the record has moved on, and when the template already carries the target it keeps the live partition rather than raising it over servers on the target (a server being replaced came back on the current revision: an extra restart, or the unpullable held target after an expansion, #562 re-walk). It waits, writing the held template back itself, while a StatefulSet created again after an expansion has not got it back (operations.md ids 162, 171). A retarget is staged at the lowest server that runs a newer revision than the StatefulSet's current one, never below it (Stage A Retarget Without Sending A Server Back, operations.md id 180). A retarget mid-flight is announced by one UpgradeRetargeted event per new target, from the write that records it (operations.md id 180). Rolling, Stabilizing and Verifying act only while the upgrade record as stored has the cached copy's phase, target and partition, and Rolling reads the server StatefulSet from the API server: a stale cache is consistently old, and a Rolling step on a StatefulSet from before Staging wrote a new target lowered the partition onto it with no check (operations.md id 203). Each Rolling pass with a replica not Ready replaces the server pods that cannot start and are due for the update (Replace Server Pods That Cannot Start, operations.md id 204). Its completion (completeUpgrade) writes the record Completed and then the cluster's Ready status and version; that write announces ClusterReady only when it takes the cluster into Ready — a walk that replaced servers which could not start on a cluster Degraded or Forming — never for a cluster that stayed Ready through its upgrade (#606; operations.md id 136). Its wait for each restarted server takes a member that is Available at the pod's address, Enabled or Cordoned: a cordoned server keeps its state across the restart, and a cluster with one is Ready (operations.md id 224).

name: Pause Or Fail Rolling Upgrade
description: Routes a failed upgrade step to Paused (manual intervention required, never auto-resumed: the user changes spec.image.tag or turns autoPauseOnFailure off) when upgradeStrategy.autoPauseOnFailure is set, or to Failed so the operator retries the upgrade once the cluster is Ready with every server available. Either way the StatefulSet keeps the partition the step left, so no server the upgrade has not rolled restarts onto the target outside the state machine. An attempt refused before Staging records the target it was for. The phase that was active when the step failed is recorded in neo4j_operator_upgrade_duration_seconds (operations.md id 149). A refusal by a check before Staging goes through Refuse Upgrade Start instead, which leaves the cluster Ready. The stop is logged once at info when its record is written, with the Warning event; it is not an ERROR, and a Failed upgrade is requeued for the normal pass rather than returned as a reconcile error (#562 re-walk). The cluster keeps its phase — Ready, its message naming the stopped upgrade — instead of turning Paused or Failed for one pass, and UpgradePaused or UpgradeFailed is announced once per target and cause: the retry of the same target keeps lastError, and a stop with the same error again is not announced. The Failed retry is kept, quiet: no ClusterReady and no UpgradeFailed on each cycle (#565; operations.md id 149). Readers of health read the upgrade record: the published Argo CD check maps a Ready cluster with a Failed upgrade to Degraded and a Paused one to Suspended, and kubectl neo4j status and diagnose flag it. The same write sets the Stalled condition True (reason UpgradeFailed or UpgradePaused), which kstatus readers such as Flux read as Failed while Ready stays True; it turns False when the upgrade goes on, completes or is dropped.

name: Hold A Stopped Upgrade
description: While an upgrade is Paused or Failed (upgradeHeld), keeps the server StatefulSet's RollingUpdate partition where the state machine left it: every normal-path apply keeps the live partition, and a StatefulSet created again (storage expansion) starts at status.upgradeStatus.currentPartition, or frozen at replicas if nothing was staged. The servers below it are not a rollout in flight, so the cluster can be Ready (or a server short) while its servers run two versions, and users, roles, databases and backups keep working. Only the state machine moves the partition: a Failed upgrade is retried once every server is available; a Paused one waits while upgradeWaitsForUser (autoPauseOnFailure set and spec.image.tag the record's target) (internal/controller/upgrade_hold.go, operations.md id 149). For a target without a patch, the held cluster's next Ready pass records what the servers at or above the partition report in status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion, so a tag below it is refused even when the upgrade paused before its availability check saw the restarted server (operations.md id 153). While it keeps a partition, a change of spec.topology.servers waits (Hold Topology During Upgrade, operations.md id 163). While it holds, each normal pass records whether a server has started on the target (an image may have become pullable), and drops the record of a held upgrade no server started on whose target spec.image.tag no longer names and whose target the StatefulSet's template does not carry, so its 'takes it up again' message goes (#562 walk; operations.md id 149).

name: Verify Version Upgrade
description: Confirms every Enabled server in SHOW SERVERS reports the target image version, applying a kernel-alias normalization for the one CalVer release (2025.01.x) that self-reports as kernel 5.27.x, before the upgrade is allowed to complete. The patch is compared only when the tag names one: a patch-less tag (5.26-enterprise, 2026.08-enterprise) floats to the newest patch of its line, so any patch of that line passes (operations.md id 149). On success it returns the highest version the Enabled servers reported, which the Completed write records as status.runningVersion for a tag without a patch (operations.md id 153).

name: Detect Split Brain
description: Queries each running server pod's own SHOW SERVERS view, groups pods that see similar cluster configurations, and flags a split-brain when a minority group's servers are not a subset of the majority group's visible servers. Runs only on a cluster that has been healthy: phase Ready or Degraded. On a Ready cluster whose server pods have not changed it runs at most every --split-brain-check-interval (default 5m; 0 runs it every pass), as decided by Verify Cluster Formation. Its per-server clients read the admin Secret the servers were given, spec.auth.adminSecret or the default neo4j-admin-secret when it is unset (getClusterAdminSecretName); they used to refuse a cluster without the field, as did the upgrade's per-server database gate, which uses the same client (operations.md id 132). Each view counts the members it lists Available, Enabled or Cordoned (operations.md id 224).

name: Restart Orphaned Pods
description: Repairs a detected split-brain by deleting the orphaned pods (or, in the nuclear-option repair action, every server pod) so the StatefulSet recreates them and they rejoin the majority cluster view.

name: Drain Server For Scale-Down
description: Drives one cordon/deallocate/wait/drop step per reconcile for servers being removed by a topology scale-down, gating on a DEALLOCATE dry-run and the system database's minimum-voting-member floor before ever cordoning a server. Each step is decided from SHOW SERVERS read on the system leader (a follower's view can lag), and a refusal saying a server is already deallocating or dropped is treated as progress, not a block (#476). The draining-servers annotation on the cluster is written as a merge patch of that annotation alone (operations.md id 150). The servers it drains are every server the scale-down removes, one that is down too: SHOW SERVERS lists a server that is down with no address and its id for a name, so its ordinal comes from the address it last reported (the address book and status.diagnostics), else by elimination when every server the scale-down keeps is named by another row; while a kept server is down and unknown as well, it drains what it can name and keeps the replicas held with ServersPendingDrain saying why, never touching a server it cannot name. A 5→3 scale-down issued while server-3's pod was being replaced drained only server-4, released the hold, and left server-3 Enabled/Unavailable for good (#594; operations.md id 213). The pass that finds nothing left to drain releases the hold and sets ServersPendingDrain False (NoServersPendingDrain) with "Scale-down drain complete"; a scale-down set back before its drain ended sets "Scale-down not in progress". Either is written only over a condition True as stored, decided in the write from the object it re-reads (settleScaleDownCondition), so the passes after a completed drain — a stale StatefulSet, the replicas lowered, a copy from before the completion's write — leave it as it is. The completion's message sat on a branch no pass could reach, and the condition always ended "not in progress" (#606; operations.md id 219). The cordon step records the servers it cordons, before CORDON, in neo4j.com/scale-down-cordoned-servers on the cluster. A scale-down set back before its drain ended gives back what the drain took: ENABLE SERVER for each recorded server still Cordoned (never one cordoned by hand), the records dropped, ServersPendingDrain False "Scale-down not in progress", one ScaleDownSetBack event; a set-back part of the way (5→3, then 4) gives back the server the spec keeps again and drains the rest. A set-back after the drain took a kept server past undoing (deallocating, deallocated, or dropped and still running) is refused: replicas held, ServersPendingDrain ScaleDownBlocked naming the servers and the spec.topology.servers that lets the drain finish. With no drain on record it asks Neo4j nothing. A 3→5→3→5 set-back within a second used to leave server-3 and server-4 Cordoned and the cluster Forming (#608; operations.md id 224).

name: Plan Scale-Down Step
description: Pure decision function that inspects the live State/Hosting of each drain-target server and picks the single next drain action (cordon, deallocate, wait, or drop) for the caller to execute — a draining server hosting only `system` is droppable even if stuck in Deallocating.

name: Expand Cluster Storage
description: Compares each server-StatefulSet PVC's current size against spec.storage.size, rejects any shrink attempt, and on growth patches the PVCs then orphan-deletes the StatefulSet so it is recreated with the updated VolumeClaimTemplates.

name: Expand Standalone Storage
description: Standalone twin of sf-expand-storage: compares the neo4j-data PVC size against spec.storage.size, rejects shrinks, and patches plus orphan-deletes the single-replica StatefulSet on growth so it is recreated with the enlarged claim template.

name: Check Storage Expansion Needed
description: Compares desired PVC storage size from spec.storage.size against the live PVCs' storage requests and reports match, expand, or shrink so the caller can decide whether to proceed, no-op, or hard-reject.

name: Calculate Topology Placement
description: Determines whether topology-spread and/or anti-affinity should be applied, auto-discovers availability zones from cluster-scoped Nodes when none are configured, and degrades to best-effort zone spread (rather than failing) when node listing is unavailable in namespace-scoped installs. The TopologyPlacementCalculated event is announced when the zones change, not on every pass (#527).

name: Apply Topology Constraints
description: Applies the calculated topology-spread constraints and/or pod anti-affinity rules onto the server StatefulSet's pod template before it is created or updated.

name: Verify Cluster Formation
description: Checks Bolt connectivity (tracking a consecutive-failure streak for outage forensics), then runs split-brain detection with a legacy SHOW SERVERS count fallback to decide whether the cluster has formed with the expected number of Enabled+Available servers. On a Ready cluster the full split-brain check is skipped, and the cluster counted formed from SHOW SERVERS through the client Service, when that lists every expected server Enabled and Available and a full check found the cluster whole within --split-brain-check-interval (default 5m) against the same server pods: none deleted, recreated, restarted or changed readiness since. Only such a clean check is recorded (in memory, per cluster); any other outcome clears the record, so the next pass checks in full. Returns the SHOW SERVERS list it saw and whether the shortfall is a split-brain, for the shortfall assessment. Its SHOW SERVERS yields each server's version too, which the Ready pass records for a tag without a patch (status.runningVersion, status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion while an upgrade is held) without a query of its own (operations.md id 153). It has no error to return: every way the check comes back short — no connection, no server list, a split-brain — is a formationCheck the shortfall assessment reads (the ClusterFormationFailed branch it fed could never run, #531). A server counts when it is a member, Enabled or Cordoned, and Available: a cordoned server keeps the databases it hosts, and a cluster with one cordoned by hand, or by a scale-down set back, read Forming with "Cluster formation verification incomplete" (#608; operations.md id 224).

name: Hold Image Drift Until Ready
description: While the cluster is not Ready, pins the in-memory spec image back to whatever the live StatefulSet currently runs so the normal reconcile path can't apply a version change outside the upgrade state machine, unless zero replicas are ready (nothing to protect: a first deploy wedged on a bad tag, or a cluster that has lost every server). The tag has already been checked against status.version, and the Ready pass records the new version once every server runs it (operations.md id 144). The image in place is the server StatefulSet's, or, while a storage expansion has orphan-deleted it, the image the highest-ordinal orphaned server pod runs, so the StatefulSet created again does not roll every server onto the held image ungated (#538). The image is split as the operator built it: a tag may carry a digest (#531). Its UpgradeDeferred is announced on the second pass that holds the same image, once, and not for a change a stopped upgrade's record already names (#550).

name: Is Upgrade Required
description: Detects image drift on the server StatefulSet (or a Failed upgrade, or a Paused one whose autoPauseOnFailure has been turned off, whose target is still spec.image.tag while status.version disagrees) to decide whether a rolling upgrade should start or be taken up again; never fires while a Paused upgrade still waits for the user (autoPauseOnFailure set and the tag unchanged), already mid-flight, or while a server is unavailable (Degraded condition True), since rolling the others could cost the cluster its majority (operations.md id 149). Exception: a held upgrade whose restarted servers cannot start on its target, with spec.image.tag moved to another image, is taken up although servers are down (operations.md id 162). An attempt at the same image a check refused before Staging is tried again only once a minute has passed, so the normal pass runs in between (id 149). A Failed upgrade is retried only once every server pod of the server StatefulSet is Ready, and not within a minute of a retry the pre-upgrade check refused: the status cannot show a server short after a stop (the upgrade stopped on a cluster that read Ready with every server available, and the normal pass does not run while the machine does), so the normal pass runs meanwhile and records the shortfall (Degraded condition, then phase Degraded past the grace), after which the unavailable-server check holds the retry until every server is back. A retry on every pass had kept the normal pass from running: a server that could not start on the target stayed hidden behind Degraded=False (walk of be1e0a6f; operations.md ids 105, 149).

name: Ensure Seed Credentials Projected
description: Validates that a hosting cluster or standalone CR's spec.extraEnvFrom projects the cloud-credentials Secret a seedURI restore needs, auto-patching it in (and triggering a rolling restart) only when the CR carries the neo4j.com/auto-inherit-seed-creds annotation. The entry and the neo4j.com/seed-creds-auto-inherited-from annotation are written as a merge patch, never an Update, so nothing else in the user's spec changes (operations.md id 150).

name: Ensure PVC Seed Proxy
description: Idempotently creates the busybox-httpd Deployment, Service, and NetworkPolicy that expose a backup PVC over HTTP so Neo4j's URLConnectionSeedProvider can seed a database from it during a restore; the policy admits only the target's server pods (a cluster's neo4j.com/cluster label, a standalone's app label). The provider fetches one file, so a differential's chain is merged first (sf-merge-seed-chain).

name: Merge PVC Backup Chain for Seeding
description: newSeedMergePlan / applySeedMerge (pvc_seed_merge.go): when a PVC seed artifact is not recorded as a FULL backup, the seed proxy pod gets a merge-chain init container running the target's Neo4j image that copies the chain to scratch space (emptyDir or spec.options.tempStorage), merges it with neo4j-admin database aggregate-backup (5.x) / backup aggregate (CalVer), and publishes the merged full artifact at the original relative path; a failed merge fails the restore at once with neo4j-admin's reason (rule 109). The merged result is checked with backup inspect --show-metadata and refused if it is a differential (5.26 reports an empty differential with no full as an existing full backup).

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves the target host, checks readiness, projects seed credentials if needed, and ensures the database exists. A host that is missing, or that lacks the seed credentials Secret, is phase Pending; ClusterNotFound, SeedCredsMissing, CreationFailed and DataImportFailed are emitted only when the status write that records them changed something (knowledge operations.md id 145). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned spec.ifNotExists and spec.wait: false into true (operations.md id 150). A host that does not exist yet is reached as the ClusterNotFound wait (Pending, one Warning): the DatabaseValidator reports it as TargetPending, not as an error (operations.md id 182). While the host is not Ready, or reads Ready but does not accept the connection (at connect, in ensureDatabase or in the initial-data import), a database Ready at its generation stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (waitForHost, hostUnreachable); one not yet Ready waits in Pending; no event and no error, and ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes. ClusterNotReady=False is written once the host served the pass — its statements answered, just before the Ready report, or where the pass stops on the wait for seed credentials, not when the connection is made (hostAnswered; operations.md id 210) — and the pass's copy takes that write (operations.md id 183). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A validation failure and the wait for the host's seed credentials are logged once per cause at info, from the status write that announces them, and at V(1) on the passes in between, never as an ERROR on every requeue (logRefusal; operations.md id 197). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). A statement Neo4j asks to be retried (targetAway: a cluster that lost the majority of its servers still reads Ready and answers Neo.TransientError.Statement.RemoteExecutionTransientError) is the same wait as an unreachable host: ClusterNotReady=True with reason ClusterUnreachable, a Ready database stays Ready, logged at info, RequeueAfter without an error, no CreationFailed, and ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes; the observation read that fails the same way keeps the last reading at info (operations.md id 210). A target CR that went away (the object had found it) is a wait at once but its ClusterNotFound Warning comes only if the object outlasts the target by a minute, so a teardown raises none (targetGoneNotices; operations.md id 216). An older live CR of its kind in the namespace that gives the same name on the same clusterRef, ignoring case (Neo4j lower-cases the names), owns it: the pass is then Failed with one DuplicateName Warning naming that CR and sends Neo4j nothing, before the target is resolved, and a watch on the kind (othersOfTheName, nameClaimChanged in duplicate_names.go) reconciles it when the owner is deleted or renamed (operations.md id 217).

name: Create Or Verify Database
description: ensureDatabase() checks DatabaseExists, which matches the name ignoring case (neo4j.FindDatabase; Neo4j lists database names lower-cased, knowledge operations.md id 146), then issues CREATE DATABASE (plain, with TOPOLOGY, or from seedURI/seedURIs via OPTIONS) and reads the database out of SHOW DATABASES (observeDatabase): state folded over every copy (online when all are, otherwise the first other status by name) and the sorted server addresses, independent of row order and matching the name ignoring case. It returns that observation for the status write instead of setting it on the in-memory CR, which the write's re-fetch discarded (knowledge operations.md id 143). resolveDatabaseCreateInputs() decides the host-dependent inputs once for every create path: spec.defaultCypherLanguage is sent as DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER only when the target image is CalVer (neo4j.DefaultLanguageForImage; the 5.26 LTS has no such clause, so it is omitted), and spec.topology is ignored for a standalone host. All four create methods render through one statement builder.

name: Alter Database Topology
description: internal/neo4j/client.go's AlterDatabaseTopology issues ALTER DATABASE `name` SET TOPOLOGY n PRIMARIES m SECONDARIES for a post-bootstrap topology change; a capability of the Neo4j client, not currently auto-invoked from the Neo4jDatabase reconcile loop (CLAUDE.md documents it as an operator-triggered change).

name: Drop Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() resolves the host and issues DROP DATABASE for spec.name, releasing the finalizer on success or on a non-retryable failure. A retryable failure keeps the finalizer and requeues: the failure is written through updateDatabaseStatus (phase Error, Ready reason DeletionFailed) and DeletionFailed is emitted only when that write changed the status, once per failure rather than on every retry (knowledge operations.md id 145). After a successful drop it lists Neo4jRoles on the same clusterRef and warns (non-fatally) on each role whose spec still grants on the dropped database, case-insensitively. A client that cannot be created for a host that exists (restarting, refusing Bolt, its admin Secret unreadable) is the same wait, no longer read as 'the database is already gone'; the release after the grace period names the database left in Neo4j and the DROP DATABASE that removes it (operations.md id 178). A finalizer release that finds the object already gone is success, logged at V(1), not an error (operations.md id 189). A DROP that meets a server name that does not resolve ('no such host': the routing table names a cluster server's pod FQDN under the headless Service, absent while the pod is replaced) is retried like any unreachable target, not read as a deployment that is gone; only a host CR that no longer exists releases at once (classifyFinalizerCleanup; operations.md id 178). When its target is being deleted or gone, the target's volumes decide (fateOfTarget, settleByTarget): being deleted or gone with its volumes (storage.retentionPolicy Delete, the default) releases at once; being deleted with its volumes kept still takes the cleanup; gone with its volumes kept waits, bounded, for a deployment created again from them, then names what they hold (operations.md id 178). A statement Neo4j asks to retry is retried quietly within the deletion's grace period, and named in the release Warning only if it lasts past it (retryTransient; operations.md id 178). While another live CR of its kind gives the same name on the same clusterRef, ignoring case, the deletion drops nothing: it releases the finalizer with one DuplicateNameKept event naming that CR, which keeps the object (keptFor in duplicate_names.go; operations.md id 217).

name: Import Initial Data
description: importInitialData() executes each spec.initialData.cypherStatements entry against the new database once, skipped when the database was created from a seedURI.

name: Update Neo4jDatabase Status
description: updateDatabaseStatus() / updateDatabaseStatusObserved() re-fetch the CR under retry.RetryOnConflict and set the Ready condition, status.phase and status.message, plus the pass's SHOW DATABASES observation (status.state, status.servers) applied to the re-fetched object. Nothing is written when the status would not change (a status write is a watch event). They report whether the Ready condition's status or reason, the phase or the message changed, from the attempt whose write succeeded; reportDatabaseReady emits DatabaseReady and the validation gate emits ValidationFailed only on that transition (knowledge operations.md ids 136, 143). The phase comes from databasePhaseFor: Ready; ValidationFailed (the api/v1beta1 constant PhaseValidationFailed); Pending for a wait (host missing, not Ready or not answering, seed credentials not on the host); Error for a retried drop during deletion; Failed for every other reason. There is no Unknown (operations.md id 190).

name: Reconcile Neo4jDatabaseAlias
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec inline, resolves clusterRef, waits for the target database to exist, then compares the live alias (if any) against spec.targetDatabase. Database and alias names are matched ignoring case, as Neo4j stores them lower-cased (knowledge operations.md id 146). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150). A clusterRef that names no cluster or standalone yet is phase Pending, Ready reason ClusterNotFound, with one ClusterNotFound Warning from the status write that enters the wait; the object carries on once the deployment exists (the requeue, or its creation enqueuing dependents). The validator no longer refuses the missing deployment first (knowledge operations.md id 182). While the target is not Ready (or reads Ready but does not accept the connection, at connect or mid-pass) an object Ready at its generation stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True — reason ClusterNotReady or ClusterUnreachable — and anything else waits in its waiting phase; no event, RequeueAfter without an error, reported as a failure only after 5 minutes; the Ready event is announced from the status write that enters Ready, never from the pass's copy (operations.md id 183). Its Neo4j calls go through the aliasNeo4jClient seam, which tests script. Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). A statement Neo4j asks to be retried (targetAway: a cluster that lost the majority of its servers still reads Ready and answers a Neo.TransientError) is the same wait, reason ClusterUnreachable, with no AliasFailed; ClusterNotReady=False is written just before the Ready write, once the statements answered, or when the pass stops because the target database does not exist yet, so the wait's clock is not reset by a connection alone (operations.md id 210). A target CR that went away (the object had found it) is a wait at once but its ClusterNotFound Warning comes only if the object outlasts the target by a minute, so a teardown raises none (targetGoneNotices; operations.md id 216). An older live CR of its kind in the namespace that gives the same name on the same clusterRef, ignoring case (Neo4j lower-cases the names), owns it: the pass is then Failed with one DuplicateName Warning naming that CR and sends Neo4j nothing, before the target is resolved, and a watch on the kind (othersOfTheName, nameClaimChanged in duplicate_names.go) reconciles it when the owner is deleted or renamed (operations.md id 217).

name: Create Alias
description: Issues CREATE ALIAS when ShowAlias, which matches the name ignoring case, reports no existing alias with this name, pinned to Cypher 5 so the server's default language cannot change how a dotted name is read.

name: Retarget Alias
description: Issues ALTER ALIAS ... SET TARGET when the live alias's database differs from spec.targetDatabase, compared ignoring case (aliasTargetDiffers; drift correction; spec wins).

name: Drop Alias On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() issues DROP ALIAS IF EXISTS unless spec.deletionPolicy=Retain, through the newDeletionClient seam. A target that is not Ready, a connection or a drop that fails keeps the finalizer and waits, announced once; after finalizerDeletionGracePeriod the finalizer is released with a Warning naming the alias left in Neo4j. A target CR that is gone releases at once. It used to wait for ever on a target that was not Ready and release at once on a failed connection or drop (operations.md id 178). A finalizer release that finds the object already gone is success, logged at V(1), not an error (operations.md id 189). When its target is being deleted or gone, the target's volumes decide (fateOfTarget, settleByTarget): being deleted or gone with its volumes (storage.retentionPolicy Delete, the default) releases at once; being deleted with its volumes kept still takes the cleanup; gone with its volumes kept waits, bounded, for a deployment created again from them, then names what they hold (operations.md id 178). A statement Neo4j asks to retry is retried quietly within the deletion's grace period, and named in the release Warning only if it lasts past it (retryTransient; operations.md id 178). While another live CR of its kind gives the same name on the same clusterRef, ignoring case, the deletion drops nothing: it releases the finalizer with one DuplicateNameKept event naming that CR, which keeps the object (keptFor in duplicate_names.go; operations.md id 217).

name: Reconcile Neo4jShardedDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves the referenced cluster, checks property-sharding readiness, opens a Neo4j client, and drives seed resolution plus create/status refresh. shardCreateNeeded decides whether CREATE DATABASE is sent: always on the destructive replaceExisting pass and while the readiness SHOW DATABASES lists no family (the virtual database and its -g000 graph shard); for a listed family only under ifNotExists: false when this CR did not create it (status.virtualDatabase does not name spec.name), so Neo4j's 'already exists' refusal surfaces instead of the family being adopted. ShardedDatabaseReady, SeedBackupPending, SeedProxyStarting and ValidationFailed are emitted only when the status write (transitionStatus) changes the phase or message. A clusterRef that names no cluster is phase Pending (ev-cluster-not-found, once), with the operator's validator wired in too: the validator reports the missing cluster as Pending, not as an error (#532); any other read error is retried with backoff. Every Warning about a lasting condition (cluster without property sharding, client creation, seedBackupRef resolution, a failed reconcile) is emitted only when the status write that records it changed the phase or message (knowledge operations.md id 145). Each pass reads the CR through the uncached APIReader (reader()), so the phase steps, shardedSeedConsumable and the destructive-restore generation guard decide from the last pass's write rather than a stale cache copy (knowledge operations.md ids 94, 136). A refused spec reads "Validation failed" once, in status and in the ValidationFailed event. transitionStatus copies the status its write stored into the pass's own copy, so a new CR's first pass writes Validating, Creating, then Ready (or the wait it meets); from its own copy it kept no phase after writing Validating and never wrote Creating (#549). From a Ready status an earlier operator left, the first pass writes and announces nothing (#553; knowledge operations.md id 136). While the cluster is not Ready with property sharding operational, or reads Ready but does not accept the connection, a sharded database Ready at its generation stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (waitForCluster, clusterUnreachable); one not yet Ready waits in Waiting; ClientCreationFailed only after 5 minutes (operations.md id 183). Its validation failure, a cluster without property sharding and an unresolvable seedBackupRef are logged once per cause at info, at V(1) after, never as an ERROR on every requeue (logRefusal; operations.md id 197). A statement Neo4j asks to be retried (targetAway: a cluster that lost the majority of its servers still reads Ready) is the same wait, reason ClusterUnreachable, with no ReconcileFailed and ClientCreationFailed only after 5 minutes; clusterAnswered writes ClusterNotReady=False before the Ready transition, once the statements answered, and where the pass stops on a seed wait (seed backup, seed proxy, seed configuration). A sharded database Ready at its generation, or already waiting out its cluster, asks for readiness once instead of thirty times a second apart, so a lost majority does not hold the reconciler's only worker thirty seconds a pass (readinessAttemptsFor; operations.md id 210). An older live CR of its kind in the namespace that gives the same name on the same clusterRef, ignoring case (Neo4j lower-cases the names), owns it: the pass is then Failed with one DuplicateName Warning naming that CR and sends Neo4j nothing, before the target is resolved, and a watch on the kind (othersOfTheName, nameClaimChanged in duplicate_names.go) reconciles it when the owner is deleted or renamed (operations.md id 217).

name: Create Sharded Database
description: createShardedDatabase() executes the statement buildCreateShardedDatabaseCypher() renders: `CYPHER 25 CREATE DATABASE ... SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 25 SET GRAPH SHARD {...} SET PROPERTY SHARDS {...} OPTIONS {...}`, binding every seed/user-supplied value as a driver parameter. The language clause is always emitted: shard sub-databases inherit the parent's language, and the server no longer forces CYPHER_25 for sharding. Called on the destructive replaceExisting pass, while SHOW DATABASES does not list the family, or under ifNotExists: false for a family this CR did not create: without IF NOT EXISTS Neo4j refuses CREATE on an existing name, which is what ifNotExists: false asks for. The keys of a per-shard seedURI map (spec.seedURIs, or the map resolved from seedBackupRef) are sent lower-cased, as Neo4j names the shards.

name: Drop Sharded Database For Replace
description: dropShardedDatabaseIfExists() issues `CYPHER 25 DROP DATABASE ... IF EXISTS DESTROY DATA WAIT`, gated to the spec.replaceExisting+force path and guarded by status.lastDestructiveRestoreGeneration so it never re-fires at the same generation.

name: Stamp Server Default Cypher Language
description: stampClusterCypherLanguage()/stampStandaloneCypherLanguage() resolve spec.serverDefaultCypherLanguage (resources.StampServerCypherLanguage) from the spec, a legacy db.query.default_language key, the existing stamp, the image line, whether the StatefulSet exists and the value in the current ConfigMap, and persist it to status.effectiveCypherLanguage before the ConfigMap that renders it is built (internal/controller/server_cypher_language.go).

name: Resolve And Serve Sharded Seed
description: resolveShardedSeed()/resolvePVCShardedSeed() turn spec.seedBackupRef into either per-shard cloud seedURIs or an operator-managed PVC seed-proxy Deployment+Service serving each shard's .backup file over HTTP. A PVC run with a shard recorded as DIFF is refused before the proxy starts (Neo4j seeds a sharded database over HTTP only from full backups, and merging drops the sharding header); the requeue seeds once a full run lands. For a cloud seed, ensureClusterSeedConfig() projects the backup's credentials and custom endpoint onto the cluster under the auto-inherit annotation and waits for the rollout. Without the annotation the database waits in phase Pending with one ev-seed-creds-missing, naming what is missing, and seeds once the cluster has it (knowledge operations.md id 145). The per-shard seedURI keys it builds, cloud and PVC, are the target's shard names lower-cased (shardSeedKey): Neo4j derives the shard names from the lower-cased database name and matches the keys exactly, so keys built from a capitalised spec.name were refused (knowledge operations.md id 146).

name: Update Shard Status
description: updateShardStatus() reads SHOW DATABASES once per reconcile and records, from those rows only, status.graphShard (`{name}-g000`), status.propertyShards (`{name}-pNNN`, ordered by index), status.virtualDatabase (the logical database) and status.creationTime (set once when the graph shard is first seen; restarted by a destructive recreate). Per-shard state is online only when every copy is online; ready means at least one copy is online and none that should be online is not. The write is skipped when nothing changed and failures are non-fatal. Shard size, servers, lastError, propertyCount, the virtual database's endpoint and metrics, and status.totalSize stay unpopulated because SHOW DATABASES does not carry them. Family names are matched case-insensitively, as Neo4j compares database names: spec.name may contain capitals, while SHOW DATABASES lists the database lower-cased.

name: Reconcile Neo4jReplicaDatabase
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves clusterRef, checks the version gate for cross-cluster replicas, then OBSERVES the live database's type (GetDatabaseInfo, which matches the name ignoring case) before dispatching on source.mode to create (backup or network), reporting, or terminally marking it promoted.
