While the database is still a replica it publishes the lag SHOW DATABASES reports (a transaction count) as neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions{namespace,cluster_name,replica,database,k8s_cluster}, and removes that series whenever it cannot vouch for it: when the CR is deleted, found gone, or promoted, when the database has vanished from the server, and when the downstream cluster is missing, not Ready or too old for replicas, the Neo4j client cannot connect, the database lookup fails, or the spec fails validation. The next successful observation sets the gauge again. The Neo4j client is obtained through an injectable factory (replicaNeo4jClient) so these branches are testable without a Bolt server. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150). A clusterRef that names no cluster or standalone yet is phase Pending, Ready reason ClusterNotFound, with one ClusterNotFound Warning from the status write that enters the wait; the object carries on once the deployment exists (the requeue, or its creation enqueuing dependents). The validator no longer refuses the missing deployment first (knowledge operations.md id 182). While the downstream target is not Ready, or reads Ready but does not accept the connection, a Replicating replica stays Replicating with ClusterNotReady=True and its lag series withdrawn (waitForTarget, unreachable); one not yet Replicating waits in Pending; ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes. ReplicaReady is announced from the write that moves it into Replicating (reportReplicating; operations.md id 183). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). A statement Neo4j asks to be retried (targetAway: a cluster that lost the majority of its servers still reads Ready and answers a Neo.TransientError) is the same wait, reason ClusterUnreachable, with no ReplicaFailed; ClusterNotReady=False is written after a create or before reportReplicating, once the statements answered, and where the pass stops on a wait of something else — the upstream, the credentials rollout, the servers' AWS_REGION — or finds the database promoted (targetServed; operations.md id 210). A target CR that went away (the object had found it) is a wait at once but its ClusterNotFound Warning comes only if the object outlasts the target by a minute, so a teardown raises none (targetGoneNotices; operations.md id 216). status.replicationLag is a pointer: 0 at zero lag (the LAG column shows 0), absent only until the operator first reads it; while the target cannot be read it keeps the last reading and the lag metric is withdrawn (operations.md id 218).

name: Create Replica Database From Backup
description: Calls CreateReplicaDatabaseFromBackup with the upstream database, pull/seed URI, and optional topology when the target database does not yet exist (source.mode: backup). pullURI is either set directly or resolved by sf-resolve-upstream-backup-ref from source.upstreamBackupRef. Before an s3:// seed it checks that the downstream servers carry AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, read from spec.env, the live server container's env, and every variable an envFrom source supplies (spec.extraEnvFrom and the live container's envFrom, with the source's prefix); a source it cannot read, or a cloud workload identity, leaves the check to the server. A missing region leaves the replica Pending with one ev-replica-object-store-env-missing, and it carries on by itself once the servers have the region (knowledge operations.md id 145).

name: Detect Out-Of-Band Promotion
description: markPromoted() records the terminal Promoted phase the moment the live database's `type` column is observed to no longer be replica, whether caused by this operator's own Neo4jReplicaPromotion or an external actor. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series, since a promoted database no longer replicates.

name: Drop Replica Database On Deletion
description: handleDeletion() re-checks the live database type and only issues DROP DATABASE while it is still type=replica; a promoted database is retained instead. Removes the replica's neo4j_operator_replica_lag_transactions series whatever the outcome. A target that is not Ready, a connection, a type read or a drop that fails keeps the finalizer and waits, announced once (a type that cannot be read is never taken for a promoted database); after finalizerDeletionGracePeriod the finalizer is released with a Warning naming the replica left in Neo4j (operations.md id 178). A finalizer release that finds the object already gone is success, logged at V(1), not an error (operations.md id 189). When its target is being deleted or gone, the target's volumes decide (fateOfTarget, settleByTarget): being deleted or gone with its volumes (storage.retentionPolicy Delete, the default) releases at once; being deleted with its volumes kept still takes the cleanup; gone with its volumes kept waits, bounded, for a deployment created again from them, then names what they hold (operations.md id 178). A statement Neo4j asks to retry is retried quietly within the deletion's grace period, and named in the release Warning only if it lasts past it (retryTransient; operations.md id 178).

name: Promote Replica Database
description: Reconcile() runs CHECK (live type=replica) -> PROMOTE (PromoteReplicaDatabase) -> CHECK (type no longer replica) -> RECORD, so a crash between the call and the status write is recovered as an idempotent success rather than a repeat promote. The terminal Completed/Failed phase latches: the first write that persists it increments neo4j_operator_replica_promotions_total{namespace,cluster_name,result,k8s_cluster} exactly once (result=success or failure) and later or stale reconciles count nothing; a successful promotion also removes the replica's lag series. The RECORD step writes status.observedLagTxIds, the replica's lag just before the promotion, as a pointer: 0 when the replica was not behind, absent until the promotion completes (operations.md id 218).

name: Reconcile Neo4jBackup
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec (including replication-source chain rules), resolves the target cluster/standalone, checks readiness/suspend, runs sharded preflight, and branches to the scheduled or one-time backup path. A one-time backup that is Completed or Failed returns before the target lookup, so a restarting target cannot reopen it; when the cached copy is not terminal the phase is read through the uncached APIReader (oneTimeBackupDone), so a pass on a copy from before the Completed write cannot start a second Job and write Failed over Completed (backup-restore.md Rule 113). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned a cloud identity's autoCreate.enabled: false into true and re-spelled resource quantities (operations.md id 150). A spec.chainFromBackup parent must name the same target; a database name matches it in any case (validateChainParent; knowledge operations.md id 146). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A target that does not exist yet is a wait in phase Waiting, announced once with ClusterNotFound from the status write that enters it, and logged at info then, V(1) after (operations.md id 198). storage.path on a PVC draws a no-effect ValidationWarning: a PVC backup writes its chain directory at the PVC's root (id 102). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). A one-time backup whose Job failed says why in status.message and its BackupFailed event: the Job's Failed condition and the exit code and last lines of the backup container of the Job's most recently failed pod (jobFailureMessage, shared with the restore; operations.md id 215).

name: Create One-Time Backup Job
description: createBackupJob() creates exactly one Kubernetes Job per Neo4jBackup CR running `neo4j-admin database backup` (invariant: Job-per-CR, never a long-running backup pod/StatefulSet). With options.splitArchivePartSize on a 2026.09+ target it adds --split-archive-part-size=<bytes>; on an older target the Job is refused with a message naming the field. With backupType AUTO (the default) a shardedDatabase-scoped backup on a PVC passes --type=FULL (effectiveBackupType): only full shard backups can seed a sharded database from a PVC. A shardedDatabase-scoped backup names its shards with the patterns "<name>-g*" "<name>-p*", the logical name lower-cased (shardedBackupPatterns), so a database that only begins with the name — a copy restored as ProductsCopy — is neither backed up nor a reason to refuse the backup (backup-restore.md Rule 48). The backup container's terminationMessagePolicy is FallbackToLogsOnError, so a failed run's termination message is the end of its log, which the failure report reads (operations.md id 215).

name: Create Scheduled Backup CronJob
description: createBackupCronJob() creates/updates one CronJob per Neo4jBackup CR with spec.schedule set; each firing spawns its own child Job (still Job-per-run, never a persistent backup pod). With backupType AUTO (the default) a shardedDatabase-scoped backup on a PVC passes --type=FULL (effectiveBackupType): only full shard backups can seed a sharded database from a PVC. The scheduled path emits BackupScheduled only when the status write changes the phase or message (which names the CronJob and its schedule), not on every reconcile. Sharded backups use the same per-shard patterns as the one-time Job (backup-restore.md Rule 48). The backup container in the CronJob's job template is FallbackToLogsOnError too, so a failed scheduled run's history entry can say why (operations.md id 215).

name: Record Backup Run Outcome
description: recordOneShotBackupRun() / reconcileScheduledHistory() observe a completed Job's conditions, parse its pod log, and append a BackupRun to status.history, deferring finalization until restore-critical artifact filenames are captured — for at most artifactCaptureGrace (5 minutes) after the Job finished, not until the Job's TTL (backup-restore.md Rule 174) — including each artifact's FULL/DIFF type (status.history[].artifactType, databaseArtifacts[].type, shardArtifacts[].type), warning when a sharded run on a PVC wrote a differential shard. Expected shard names are the sharded database's spec.name lower-cased and are matched against the log ignoring case, as neo4j-admin writes them (backup-restore.md Rule 53). BackupCompleted and the Job-failed BackupFailed are emitted from the status write that enters the phase. updateBackupStatus stamps lastRunTime/lastSuccessTime when the backup enters Running/Completed and sends nothing when the status would not change (knowledge operations.md id 122). A failed run's history entry carries why it failed in BackupRun.error — the Job's reason and the backup container's exit code and last lines — for one-time runs and for scheduled CronJob children alike (operations.md id 215).

name: Parse Backup Pod Log
description: neo4jbackup_log_parser.go's regex-based parsers extract per-shard/per-database .backup filenames, sizes, whether each artifact is FULL or DIFF (from neo4j-admin's 'full/differential backup of database' lines; an AUTO run that fell back to a full is FULL), and neo4j-admin backup validate results from a completed backup pod's stdout. A database named in spec is matched against the log ignoring case. Per-shard names from the log are merged into the expected shard list ignoring case (mergeShardArtifactsFromLog).

name: Cleanup Backup Artifacts
description: cleanupBackupArtifacts() runs an alpine-based cleanup Job (deterministic UID-derived name) enforcing spec.retention (maxCount/maxAge) against a PVC-backed chain directory; cloud storage retention is delegated to bucket lifecycle rules. Counts *.backup artifacts but deletes each one together with its split-archive parts (x.backup.*).

name: Reconcile Neo4jRestore
description: Main reconcile loop: resolves the target, checks terminal phases and version compatibility, and either polls in-flight progress or starts a fresh restore attempt. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned a cloud identity's autoCreate.enabled: false into true; its own bookkeeping annotations (cypher-restore-issued, restore-pre-hooks-ran, point-in-time-path, seed-proxy-wait-started, ...) and the restore-in-progress annotation on a standalone target are merge patches too (operations.md id 150). Each pass records the restore's advisories as ValidationWarning, announced when they start to apply: spec fields nothing reads (RestoreNoEffectWarnings) and a PVC backupPath that starts with the /backup mount path, which the operator adds itself (RestorePVCPathWarnings; backup-restore.md Rule 44). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A restore Completed or Failed at its generation returns before its target is looked up, so a target deleted and created again does not reopen or re-run it; a target that does not exist yet is a wait in Pending, announced once with ClusterNotFound (operations.md id 198). storage.path on a PVC source draws a no-effect ValidationWarning (id 102). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). A Neo4j version the operator does not support is a refusal: Failed with the reason, logged once at info by logRefusal, no error returned (refuseRestore). The Ready condition carries a restore's reasons — RestoreCompleted, RestoreFailed, RestoreRunning, Pending — from restoreReadyCondition in transitionRestoreStatus, not the backup's BackupSucceeded or the generic ReconciliationFailed. A failed restore Job's status.message and RestoreFailed event say why: the Job's Failed condition and the exit code and last lines of its last failed pod's restore container, whose termination message falls back to its log (restoreJobFailure; operations.md id 215). A restore that has ended at its generation is quiet: every resync (every 30 seconds in dev mode), an event of its Job and an operator restart still run the pass, which returns at the terminal guard (restoreEndedAtGeneration) with no requeue and no write, and logs "Restore already completed" or "Restore previously failed; not retrying ..." at V(1) only — at info it was one line every 30 seconds for as long as the restore was kept (#606). A restore without spec.instanceRef is a refusal checked after that guard: Failed with "spec.instanceRef is required", written and logged at info once (refuseRestore), where every pass logged it at info and wrote its status again (operations.md id 215).

name: Start Restore
description: startRestore() validates the request, pins the resolved backup source onto status, and routes it: online (Cypher recreate/create with a seedURI, or the all-databases loop) for every cluster and for most standalone restores; the offline neo4j-admin Job (stopping the instance first when spec.stopCluster is set) only for a standalone restore that cannot be seeded online — point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity, or a Job restore already holding the instance (rule 108). A Job restore announces one RestoreStarted, "Restore job … started" with the offline reason in it (restoreJobStartedMessage), when the status write that makes the restore Running changed it — after its checks have passed (existence check, pre-restore hooks, and the stop or, with stopCluster false, the refusal of a running standalone), so a refused restore, a restore that waits in Pending, and a pass on a stale copy that finds the Job (AlreadyExists) announce nothing. The offline reason used to be a RestoreStarted of its own, at the stop with stopCluster true (two events for one restore, #573; knowledge operations.md id 145). With source.pointInTime it pins the earliest run that started at or after it (restoreRunIndex) and decides the point-in-time path before routing. A refused spec — validation (database: system, a missing backupRef), a database that exists without replaceExisting, an offline restore into a running standalone without stopCluster — is Failed with its reason, logged once at info, with no returned error and so no "Reconciler error"; a read that fails on the way stays an ERROR (refuseRestore, restoreRefusal; operations.md id 215).

name: Route Restore Online or Offline
description: standaloneOfflineReason() / restoreRunsOffline() / restoreOnJobPath() (restore_target.go) decide, from the pinned status.resolvedSource, whether a restore runs online or takes the offline neo4j-admin Job: a cluster never takes the Job; a standalone does only for point-in-time, source.type storage, an unrecorded artifact, cloud storage with no credentialsSecretRef, or a Job restore that already holds its neo4j.com/restore-in-progress marker. The reason is reported in the refusal and the RestoreStarted event (rule 108). A standalone with spec.podServiceAccountAnnotations restores from cloud storage without a credentialsSecretRef online; a restore stays on the path it started on (restore-in-progress marker → Job, cypher-restore-issued or databaseResults → online). A restore with source.pointInTime runs online only as recorded once per attempt by decidePointInTimePath() in the neo4j.com/point-in-time-path annotation (CalVer, cloud storage, a covering run, a database that does not exist); a cluster that cannot fails with the reason.

name: Create Offline Standalone Restore Job
description: createRestoreJob() builds and creates the offline `neo4j-admin database restore` Job used only for a Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone restore that cannot run online (rule 108: point-in-time, a source.type storage path, cloud storage by pod identity) (neo4j-admin restore --overwrite-destination is documented as unsafe on clusters). --from-path names the exact artifact whenever it is known (backupPath ending in .backup, or the pinned snapshot's recorded file or per-database entry for the source database) — the only form neo4j-admin restores under a different name; otherwise it globs the source database's newest file (PVC) — `<database>-<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.backup` with the name lower-cased, as neo4j-admin writes it, so a capitalised spec.database finds its artifacts and another database whose name begins with it is never taken (latestArtifactSubstitution; knowledge operations.md id 146) — or passes the cloud directory (same name only). Each attempt runs a Job of its own: the Job carries the restore's generation in the annotation neo4j.com/restore-attempt, and a Job under the restore's Job name that is terminating, controlled by another Neo4jRestore, or from an earlier attempt is never adopted — clearEarlierRestoreJob deletes it (whatever its state) and waits up to 10s for the name, and while it is still there the attempt goes Pending (errStaleRestoreJob). This attempt's own Job, created by a racing pass, is adopted on AlreadyExists (restoreJobOfThisAttempt; backup-restore.md Rule 46). The deletion used to run only while the restore read Failed, so a retry that came back through Pending adopted the terminating failed Job, and a Completed restore run again adopted its completed Job (#565). The restore container's terminationMessagePolicy is FallbackToLogsOnError, so a failed run's termination message is the end of its log, which the failure report reads (operations.md id 215).

name: Online Cypher Restore
description: startClusterCypherRestore() restores one database online against the running DBMS — on a cluster and on a standalone (rule 108): dbms.[cluster.]recreateDatabase with a seedURI over an existing database (DatabaseExists, matching the name ignoring case), CREATE DATABASE … OPTIONS {seedURI} for a new one, then polls SHOW DATABASE until every allocation is online. Target-specific plumbing (StatefulSet name, pod labels for the seed proxy's NetworkPolicy, the CR that carries seed spec.env/extraEnvFrom) comes from restoreTarget. A PVC differential is merged by the seed proxy first (the proxy serves one file over HTTP; Neo4j refuses a DIFF without its chain); it runs pre-restore hooks before issuing and post-restore hooks once online; never a Job on cluster targets. Into a standalone by pod identity, awaitSeedIdentity() holds the seed until the pod runs under its identity ServiceAccount. A point-in-time restore creates the database with seedRestoreUntil (CreateDatabaseWithSeedURIUntil) and never recreates an existing one. When the target's server pods lack the cloud seed credentials or endpoint and the target is not opted in, awaitSeedConfig() holds the restore Pending (before any hook or database action) and it carries on once they are there; SeedEndpointNotProjected is announced when transitionRestoreStatus's write changed the phase or message, not from the pass's own copy. What a restore writes into that CR (spec.env, spec.extraEnvFrom, annotations) is a merge patch of those fields (updateTargetSpec; operations.md id 150). Its one RestoreStarted (onlineRestoreStartedMessage) says, for a standalone restored online with stopCluster true, that the field is ignored — that notice was a second RestoreStarted. A database that exists without replaceExisting, a type=storage restore without source.storage or a .backup file, and an unsupported storage type are refusals: Failed, logged once at info, no returned error. Its Neo4j calls go through the onlineRestoreClient seam (onlineClient), which tests script (operations.md id 215).

name: All-Databases Restore Loop
description: startAllDatabasesRestore() drives one per-database CREATE/recreate-with-seedURI action per reconcile pass from the resolved backup's per-database artifact map, on clusters and standalones, tracking progress in status.databaseResults; runs pre-restore hooks once per attempt (neo4j.com/restore-pre-hooks-ran) and post-restore hooks before Completed, has the seed proxy merge each database's PVC chain that is not recorded as FULL, and stamps status.completionTime. Property-sharded families are excluded and must restore via their own Neo4jShardedDatabase CR. Into a standalone by pod identity, awaitSeedIdentity() holds the seed until the pod runs under its identity ServiceAccount. Missing cloud seed credentials or endpoint hold it Pending (awaitSeedConfig()) before the first database is seeded, and it carries on once they are there. The restore announces its start once, from the markDatabaseResult write that makes it Running (how many databases, the first ten by name), and each database written Failed once, as the Warning RestoreDatabaseFailed; a database starting is recorded in status.databaseResults only — one RestoreStarted per database outran the event budget (13 of 30 reached the API, #573). RestoreDatabaseFailed and RestoreSeedProgress go through ProgressRecorder (source neo4j-restore-progress), an event budget of its own; RestoreSeedProgress is one summary per restore — restored and failed so far, the database being seeded, its progress and how long it has shown it — on the first seed poll and every 10 minutes after (seedProgressEvents, seedProgressSummary), so every one is delivered. The outcome is one RestoreCompleted or RestoreFailed from the status write that changed the phase (finishAllDatabasesRestore), which the per-database events cannot crowd out of the restore's budget (knowledge operations.md id 166). The Neo4j client is reached through allDatabasesRestoreClient so a test can script it. A connection to the target, or a DatabaseExists check, that fails because the target cannot serve it for a moment — unreachable or a transient Neo4j error, such as the DatabaseUnavailable that recreating neo4j over itself causes — is a wait: the restore keeps its phase and its databases' results, records ClusterNotReady=True (ClusterUnreachable), logs at info and resumes where it was; past 5 minutes it raises one ConnectionFailed Warning and goes on waiting (awaitAllDatabasesTarget). RestoreStarted is announced only while no database of the attempt has left Pending, so a wait mid-way never announces a second start (operations.md id 206).

name: Handle Restore Success
description: handleRestoreSuccess() restarts a stopped cluster, registers/starts the restored database(s) (or all restored databases), runs post-restore hooks, and forces a cross-server recreate-from-seed so every server converges on the restored server-0 data.

name: Resolve Cluster Reference
description: ResolveClusterRef() looks up a clusterRef, trying Neo4jEnterpriseCluster first and falling back to Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone of the same name, returning a ResolvedTarget with IsReady()/NewClient() helpers. IsReady() accepts a cluster whose phase is Ready or Degraded, or whose Ready condition is True (clusterAcceptsWork), so dependents keep working against a cluster that is serving with a majority of its servers.

name: Resolve Backup Reference
description: ResolveBackupRef() dereferences a Neo4jBackup CR name into a concrete StorageLocation and the BackupsPath of its most recent Succeeded run, returning a wrapped ErrBackupNotReady when no Succeeded run exists yet.

name: Reconcile Neo4jUser
description: Drives a Neo4jUser to its desired state each loop: validates the spec (routing a not-yet-applied password Secret to Pending, not Failed), resolves the clusterRef target, creates or ALTERs the Neo4j user over Bolt (the home database compared with SHOW USERS ignoring case), diffs granted vs. desired roles and issues GRANT/REVOKE ROLE, then records RolesSynced/PasswordSynced conditions and the Ready phase. A desired role counts as existing when it is built in, granted, a Neo4jRole CR or listed by SHOW ROLES (a role created in Neo4j directly), so such a role is granted (missingRoles; operations.md id 17). While the target is not Ready a Ready user stays Ready with ClusterNotReady=True (waitForTarget), and UserReady is announced from the write that enters Ready (operations.md id 158). A retried DROP USER on deletion is written to status and announced once (id 145). The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it (operations.md id 150). CR names in spec.roles that resolve to another Neo4j role name are recorded in the RoleNamesResolved condition (reportResolvedRoles), and RolesResolved is emitted only when that mapping appears or changes (operations.md id 136). Its Neo4j calls go through the userNeo4jClient seam, which tests script. A connection failure to a target that reads Ready but cannot be reached — at connect or mid-pass — is the rest of the target's outage: the same wait with reason ClusterUnreachable, logged at info, retried on the fixed interval without an error, reported as ConnectionFailed only after 5 minutes (unreachable; operations.md id 172). The password's change token is recorded by a status write right after the statement that applied it (passwordApplied), which announces PasswordRotated, so a pass a failing grant stops does not send the same ALTER again (operations.md id 15). A clusterRef that names no cluster or standalone yet is phase Pending, Ready reason ClusterNotFound, with one ClusterNotFound Warning from the status write that enters the wait; the object carries on once the deployment exists (the requeue, or its creation enqueuing dependents). The validator no longer refuses the missing deployment first (knowledge operations.md id 182). Its deletion waits, bounded, while its cleanup cannot run, and releases the finalizer at once only when the target CR is gone (deletionCleanup in deletion_wait.go; operations.md id 178). While its target is not Ready or cannot be reached, a status that records an outcome of its own for its generation (Ready, a failure, a wait on something other than the target) is kept, so the same outcome after the restart is not announced again; a finalizer release that finds the object gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). When its target is being deleted or gone, the target's volumes decide (fateOfTarget, settleByTarget): being deleted or gone with its volumes (storage.retentionPolicy Delete, the default) releases at once; being deleted with its volumes kept still takes the cleanup; gone with its volumes kept waits, bounded, for a deployment created again from them, then names what they hold (operations.md id 178). A statement Neo4j asks to retry (Neo.TransientError.*, NotALeader) is retried quietly after 5s — logged at info, nothing on status, no event — while the object's streak of such errors is younger than five minutes (transientStreaks), on deletion within the deletion's grace period (operations.md ids 164, 178). A target CR that went away (the object had found it) is a wait at once but its ClusterNotFound Warning comes only if the object outlasts the target by a minute, so a teardown raises none (targetGoneNotices; operations.md id 216).

name: Create Neo4j user
description: CreateUserAdvanced issues CREATE USER `name` IF NOT EXISTS with staged SET PASSWORD/SET STATUS/SET HOME DATABASE/SET AUTH clauses against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Alter Neo4j user
description: AlterUser issues ALTER USER with REMOVE clauses ordered before SET clauses (password, password-change-required, suspended status, home database, external auth providers) against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j user
description: DropUserIfExists issues DROP USER `name` IF EXISTS against the system database, making user removal idempotent (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Grant role to user
description: GrantRoleToUser issues GRANT ROLE `role` TO `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke role from user
description: RevokeRoleFromUser issues REVOKE ROLE `role` FROM `user` against the system database (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Create Neo4j role
description: CreateRoleAdvanced issues CREATE ROLE `name` [IF NOT EXISTS] [AS COPY OF `copyOf`] against the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Drop Neo4j role
description: DropRoleIfExists issues DROP ROLE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database; built-in roles are never dropped by any caller (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Apply privilege statement
description: ExecutePrivilegeStatement runs the role's original (non-canonicalised) GRANT/DENY privilege statement text as auto-commit Cypher against the system database, with bounded retry on transient GQLSTATUS 25N11 conflicting-transaction errors (internal/neo4j/client.go).

name: Revoke privilege statement
description: Runs a REVOKE statement derived textually from the role's currently-applied GRANT/DENY command via DerivePrivilegeRevoke (internal/neo4j/privileges.go) through ExecutePrivilegeStatement — REVOKEs are never accepted directly from Neo4jRole.spec.privileges, and immutable privileges are skipped rather than attempted.

name: Show role privileges
description: ShowRolePrivileges runs SHOW ROLE `name` PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS YIELD command, immutable (falling back to a legacy projection without immutable on older Neo4j) to read a role's currently-applied privilege set from the system database (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Create or replace auth rule
description: CreateOrReplaceAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 CREATE OR REPLACE AUTH RULE `name` SET CONDITION <expr> SET ENABLED true|false against the system database, subsuming ALTER semantics by replacing the rule outright (and clearing its prior role grants) (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Grant roles to auth rule
description: GrantRolesToAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 GRANT ROLES r1, r2, ... TO AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Revoke roles from auth rule
description: RevokeRolesFromAuthRule issues CYPHER 25 REVOKE ROLES r1, r2, ... FROM AUTH RULE `name` against the system database (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Drop auth rule
description: DropAuthRuleIfExists issues CYPHER 25 DROP AUTH RULE `name` IF EXISTS against the system database during Neo4jAuthRule deletion cleanup (internal/neo4j/auth_rules.go).

name: Validate Neo4jUser spec
description: UserValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j username shape/length, requires at least one auth provider (passwordSecretRef or externalAuth), rejects the reserved 'system' username and the 'native' externalAuth provider, WARNS (without rejecting) when the username is the default bootstrap admin 'neo4j' because managing it rewrites the credential the operator itself authenticates with, and reports a not-yet-applied password Secret as a transient Pending gap rather than a Failed error (internal/validation/user_validator.go). A clusterRef that names no Neo4jEnterpriseCluster or Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone yet is TargetPending (validation.DeploymentPending), never an error, and every other rule still runs; a read that fails otherwise is a warning (internal/validation/deployment_ref.go; operations.md id 182). It also WARNS when the username is the one the operator signs in to the target as — the username in the target's admin Secret (NEO4J_AUTH user first, then the username key), else neo4j — and spec.roles do not grant admin (by name, or through a Neo4jRole CR of the same target whose role name is admin): spec.roles is authoritative, so the operator would revoke admin from its own login and every CR on that target would fail with Forbidden (operations.md id 211).

name: Validate Neo4jRole spec
description: RoleValidator.Validate enforces the Neo4j role-name pattern, requires spec.adoptBuiltin=true to manage a built-in role name, requires every spec.privileges entry to start with GRANT/DENY and end with `TO <this role>`, and rejects property-based-access-control privileges that target a Neo4jShardedDatabase (internal/validation/role_validator.go). A clusterRef that names no Neo4jEnterpriseCluster or Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone yet is TargetPending (validation.DeploymentPending), never an error, and every other rule still runs; a read that fails otherwise is a warning (internal/validation/deployment_ref.go; operations.md id 182).

name: Validate Neo4jRoleBinding spec
description: RoleBindingValidator.Validate enforces the shared username shape check, requires spec.roles to be non-empty with no blank entries, and warns (never errors) when PUBLIC is listed since it is implicit and always ignored (internal/validation/rolebinding_validator.go). A clusterRef that names no Neo4jEnterpriseCluster or Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone yet is TargetPending (validation.DeploymentPending), never an error, and every other rule still runs; a read that fails otherwise is a warning (internal/validation/deployment_ref.go; operations.md id 182).

name: Validate Neo4jAuthRule spec
description: AuthRuleValidator.Validate enforces the auth-rule name pattern, requires spec.condition to be a pure expression free of DDL keywords (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/GRANT/DENY/REVOKE/SHOW/RENAME/semicolon) to block Cypher injection, and requires at least one entry in spec.grantedRoles (internal/validation/authrule_validator.go). A clusterRef that names no Neo4jEnterpriseCluster or Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone yet is TargetPending (validation.DeploymentPending), never an error, and every other rule still runs; a read that fails otherwise is a warning (internal/validation/deployment_ref.go; operations.md id 182).

name: Validate spec.config
description: ConfigValidator.ValidateConfigMap, shared by the cluster and the standalone validator (and so by kubectl neo4j validate): refuses removed 4.x keys and families, the keys the operator manages itself (discovery, advertised addresses, topology, SSL policy, db.format), line breaks in values, and, for the settings in typedSettings whose type is identical on the 5.26 LTS and CalVer (memory, transaction log, checkpoints, timeouts, query logging, Bolt thread pool, routing, authentication), a value Neo4j would refuse at startup or one below a documented minimum, reported on spec.config[<key>] with the expected format and an example (ValidateSettingValues, internal/validation/setting_values.go; operations.md id 140). A cluster with property sharding enabled also has spec.propertySharding.config checked. The readers mirror Neo4j's own parsers (ByteUnit.parse, TimeUtil.parseTimeMillis, Integer/Long.parseLong, equalsIgnoreCase) and never refuse a spelling they do not model; unlisted settings, $(command) values and backslash escapes pass. The memory rules (heap plus page cache within the memory limit) read sizes with the same byte-size reader.

name: Reconcile AuraInstance
description: Top-level AuraInstanceReconciler.Reconcile loop: handles the paused annotation, then deletion (which resolves the credentials only to call Aura, operations.md id 157), then resolves credentials and the finalizer; a terminal create refusal already on status for the current generation stops the pass before Aura is called (refusalStands, id 156); dispatches to create/adopt, drift, tier-upgrade, pause/resume and deletion, then writes status.atProvider plus the Ready/Synced conditions. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156). fail() writes phase Error with the Ready condition. Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199).

name: Create or adopt Aura instance
description: observeOrCreate: lists instances by name to adopt before creating (avoiding a duplicate paid instance), validates the type/region/cloudProvider combo against the project's instance_configurations, and creates via v1 CreateInstance or, when spec.multiDatabase is true, via v2beta1 CreateInstanceV2 (createMultiDatabaseInstance in aura_multidatabase.go). A 429, a 5xx or a transport failure of the list or the create is marked where the call failed (retryableAuraCall) and retried without a status write; everything else, the operator's own errors included, is recorded as CreateFailed (operations.md id 88).

name: Resize/patch Aura instance
description: reconcileDrift: PATCHes memory, storage, name, secondariesCount and cdcEnrichmentMode when they diverge from the observed instance, gated by the Update management policy.

name: Pause Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls PauseInstance when spec.paused=true and the observed instance is running.

name: Resume Aura instance
description: reconcilePauseResume: calls ResumeInstance when spec.paused=false and the observed instance is paused.

name: Upgrade Aura instance tier
description: reconcileUpgrade: performs the single supported in-place tier upgrade (professional-db to business-critical) via UpgradeInstance when spec.type requests it; the CRD's CEL transition rule already rejects every other type change.

name: Delete/orphan Aura instance
description: handleDeletion: honours deletionPolicy before releasing the finalizer. Orphan, the default, leaves the cloud instance running and needs no credentials; Delete calls DeleteInstance unless deletionProtection is set, resolving the credentials only then. A Delete that cannot resolve them records CredentialsUnavailable and retries, and after finalizerDeletionGracePeriod (5 minutes) releases the finalizer with a Warning AuraInstanceOrphaned (operations.md id 157). A finalizer release that finds the object already gone is success, logged at V(1), not an error (operations.md id 189). A DELETE Aura refuses — not a conflict, not transient, not "not found" — is waited on the same way: reason DeletionRefused, announced once, asked again until finalizerDeletionGracePeriod has passed, then the finalizer is released with the kind's Orphaned Warning (operations.md id 201).

name: Reconcile AuraSnapshot
description: AuraSnapshotReconciler.Reconcile: requests a snapshot exactly once via CreateSnapshot, then polls GetSnapshot until Completed/Failed/Cancelled; the create response carries only snapshot_id so the initial phase is recorded as Pending rather than copying fields that are not yet present. A create or a poll Aura refuses (not a 409, not transient) goes through fail(): phase Error with the Ready condition, one AuraSnapshotFailed Warning, retried every 30s; a snapshot in a terminal phase (Completed, Failed, Cancelled) is not read again (operations.md id 156).

name: Reconcile AuraRestore
description: AuraRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target AuraInstance and a snapshot (spec.snapshotId or an AuraSnapshot ref), waits for the instance to be Running, calls RestoreSnapshot, then drives Pending->Restoring->Completed/Failed and never re-fires once terminal.

name: Reconcile AuraDatabase
description: AuraDatabaseReconciler.Reconcile: resolves org/project/instance coordinates from the referenced AuraInstance (which must have been created with multiDatabase:true), refuses creation when the instance's probed multiDatabase verdict is explicitly false, and otherwise creates/adopts the database by the external-database-id annotation since the v2beta1 API returns no database names to adopt by. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). The InstanceNotMultiDatabase refusal, once on status for the current generation and the same Aura instance ID, is not asked again; a transient failure of the list or the create is retried without a status write; AuraDatabaseReady is announced when the database becomes Ready (ids 88, 136, 156). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A terminating database is handled before its target is resolved: Orphan calls nothing; under Delete an AuraInstance CR that is gone releases the finalizer at once with a Warning AuraDatabaseOrphaned, anything else that cannot be resolved waits (CredentialsUnavailable) finalizerDeletionGracePeriod, then releases with that Warning (operations.md ids 157, 202). A DELETE Aura refuses — not a conflict, not transient, not "not found" — is waited on the same way: reason DeletionRefused, announced once, asked again until finalizerDeletionGracePeriod has passed, then the finalizer is released with the kind's Orphaned Warning (operations.md id 201). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199).

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseBackup
description: AuraDatabaseBackupReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the target database via spec.databaseRef, takes the backup exactly once via CreateDatabaseBackup, then polls GetDatabaseBackup, treating only Completed/Failed as terminal and never inferring completion from an empty just-scheduled status. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). A 429, a 5xx, a transport failure or a 409 of the backup create is retried, not recorded as BackupFailed (id 88). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156).

name: Reconcile AuraDatabaseRestore
description: AuraDatabaseRestoreReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the database and backup (by spec.backupId or an AuraDatabaseBackup ref), persists a Submitting marker before calling RestoreDatabase (the destructive, non-idempotent call), and records Submitted (not Completed, since v2beta1 exposes no way to observe restore completion) or RestoreOutcomeUnknown if the process died mid-flight.

name: Reconcile Aura org/project member
