name: Validate Aura credentials
description: AuraProviderConfigReconciler.Reconcile: resolves the referenced credentials Secret, forces a token exchange and a real ListInstances call to prove the credentials work, and reports CredentialsValidated/CredentialsInvalid on the Ready condition, re-checking every 10 minutes (auraProviderConfigRecheck; the operator wires no RequeueAfter, which had made it 30s). Each event is announced when the Ready condition changes; the condition's message leaves Aura's request ID out (operations.md ids 136, 145, 184).

name: Validate Neo4jEnterpriseCluster spec
description: ClusterValidator.ValidateWithWarnings, called on every reconcile pass and by `kubectl neo4j validate`: the spec rules (topology, image, storage, TLS, auth, spec.config keys and values, memory, spec.upgradeStrategy timeouts as Go durations above zero, MCP, Aura Fleet Management, network policy, CCDR, admin password shape) plus the rules that need the running cluster: spec.image.tag against status.version, the version every server runs, and, while an upgrade is unfinished (in flight, Paused or Failed), against status.upgradeStatus.startedTargetVersion, the newest version a server it restarted has started on, so no tag rolls such a server back; a server whose image could not be pulled never started, so the tag may go back below the target. A record an earlier operator wrote, without that field, is held to status.upgradeStatus.targetVersion once its progress says it restarted a server (operations.md id 149). A tag pinned to a digest (2026.08.1-enterprise@sha256:...) is read as its tag's version. It refuses a downgrade, CalVer to 5.x, CalVer from a 5.x other than 5.26, and 4.x, following Neo4j's upgrade guide; it does not judge an empty or unparseable status.version. A tag without a patch (5.26-enterprise) floats to the newest patch of its line and is not ordered against a patch of it, so the tag is also held to what the servers report: status.runningVersion for status.version, and status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion for an upgrade that has restarted a server; until one is recorded such a patch is not checked (operations.md id 153). There is no webhook and so no previous spec: the old update path read the cluster again and compared it with itself, so its rules never fired (operations.md id 139). The server count has no running-state rule: at least 2 servers is a spec rule, a scale-down is the drain's, and capacity for a scale-up is the scheduler's. The rolling-upgrade state machine calls the same version rule (ValidateVersionUpgrade) before it starts an upgrade (internal/validation/cluster_validator.go, upgrade_validator.go). The reconciler and the CLI apply ApplyDefaults first, to their own copy, which nothing writes back. ApplyDefaults adds no field an error can be reported on (no nameless spec.tls.issuerRef) and replaces no value the user set: it fills in the CRD's defaults (a tls block without a mode is cert-manager, as the API server stores it), takes no tls block as disabled and no service block as a ClusterIP Service, and gives the auth provider lists Neo4j's default, native, when no authentication provider is named, the authorization list only when the user set it nowhere, in spec.auth or spec.config (operations.md id 150). NoEffectWarnings says that Recreate on a cluster does what RollingUpgrade does (operations.md id 144). spec.auraFleetManagement.enabled is refused on a spec.image.tag whose entrypoint does not list fleet-management (5.26.0–5.26.10, 2025.01–2025.07), naming 5.26.11 and 2025.08.0 (operations.md id 191). An image change a Managed Neo4jPlugin of it cannot follow is refused on spec.image.tag (ManagedPluginsImageChangeErrors, internal/validation/plugin_image_change.go): a tag other than status.version while a Managed, enabled plugin not being deleted runs on status.version and not on the tag (ManagedPluginImageErrors: a name the new image's entrypoint does not list, or n10s from 5.26.22 and on early CalVer), so no server restarts on an image it would not start on; the error names the plugin and says to change it first (delete it, spec.enabled: false, or installMode: VerifiedDownload with a JAR built for the new release) and leave the tag: a server the upgrade restarts before the plugin's own write fails on the name and is replaced by that write, which a server failing on it does not wait for. A deployment already on an image the plugin cannot run is not held to it, nor is anything judged without a client (offline) (operations.md id 187). A shared procedure or extension list its spec.env reads from a Secret or ConfigMap is a ValidationWarning: it stays the cluster's variable, and its plugins cannot add their entries to it (SpecEnvListWarnings, operations.md id 209). With Aura Fleet Management enabled on an image whose entrypoint installs the plugin (not 2026.03+), a spec.env NEO4J_PLUGINS read from a Secret or ConfigMap, or a value that is not a JSON list, is a ValidationWarning: the operator cannot add fleet-management to it (FleetPluginsEnvWarnings, operations.md id 223).

name: Validate Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone spec
description: StandaloneValidator.Validate, called on every standalone reconcile pass and by `kubectl neo4j validate`: the spec rules (ValidateCreate: name length, licence, image, storage, TLS, auth, spec.config, memory, MCP, Aura Fleet Management, trusted CAs, extra volumes), the admin password's shape read from its Secret (skipped without a client, as offline), and spec.image.tag against status.version, the version the standalone runs, with the cluster's rule: a downgrade, CalVer to 5.x, CalVer from a 5.x other than 5.26 and 4.x are refused, saying 'the standalone runs'. An empty status.version is not judged. For a status.version without a patch the tag is also held to status.runningVersion, the version the server reports (operations.md id 153). There is no update-only method: ValidateUpdate, which compared an old spec with a new one, was never called (no webhook, no old object) and was deleted (internal/validation/standalone_validator.go; operations.md id 144). Its NoEffectWarnings (ValidationWarning, never an error) include spec.upgradeStrategy.upgradeTimeout, healthCheckTimeout and stabilizationTimeout set to anything but their CRD defaults: they bound steps of a cluster's rolling upgrade that a standalone's upgrade does not have (postUpgradeHealthCheck has no warning: false says what happens, true is the default; operations.md id 102). spec.auraFleetManagement.enabled is refused on a spec.image.tag whose entrypoint does not list fleet-management (5.26.0–5.26.10, 2025.01–2025.07), naming 5.26.11 and 2025.08.0 (operations.md id 191). An image change a Managed Neo4jPlugin of the standalone cannot follow is refused on spec.image.tag (ManagedPluginsImageChangeErrors, internal/validation/plugin_image_change.go): a tag other than status.version while a Managed, enabled plugin not being deleted runs on status.version and not on the tag (ManagedPluginImageErrors: a name the new image's entrypoint does not list, or n10s from 5.26.22 and on early CalVer), so no server restarts on an image it would not start on; the error names the plugin and says to change it first (delete it, spec.enabled: false, or installMode: VerifiedDownload with a JAR built for the new release) and leave the tag: a server the upgrade restarts before the plugin's own write fails on the name and is replaced by that write, which a server failing on it does not wait for. A deployment already on an image the plugin cannot run is not held to it, nor is anything judged without a client (offline) (operations.md id 187). A standalone that shares its name with a cluster has no plugins of its own: a plugin resolves its clusterRef to the cluster first. A shared procedure or extension list its spec.env reads from a Secret or ConfigMap is a ValidationWarning: Neo4j's entrypoint writes it in place of the whole list, without the standalone's spec.config, Aura Fleet Management and plugin entries (SpecEnvListWarnings, operations.md id 209). With Aura Fleet Management enabled on an image whose entrypoint installs the plugin (not 2026.03+), a spec.env NEO4J_PLUGINS read from a Secret or ConfigMap, or a value that is not a JSON list, is a ValidationWarning: the operator cannot add fleet-management to it (FleetPluginsEnvWarnings, operations.md id 223).

name: Call Aura API (shared client)
description: auraClientForCreds / resolveClient family: returns a shared *aura.Client per credential (keyed by baseURL+clientID+sha256(secret)[:8]) with one OAuth token cache and rate-limit budget (default 25/min), instrumented via metrics.RecordAuraAPICall, that every Aura reconciler's ClientFactory wraps to call ListInstances/CreateInstance/PatchInstance/GetSnapshot/etc. A caller that gets one error back from several steps retries quietly only what retryableAuraCall marked at the Aura call (aura.IsTransient also calls the operator's own errors transient; operations.md id 88).

name: Reconcile AuraCustomerManagedKey
description: AuraCustomerManagedKeyReconciler.Reconcile: adopts an existing key by matching keyId/region/cloudProvider/instanceType (the LIST endpoint returns only summaries, so each name-matched candidate is fetched by GetCustomerManagedKey to confirm before adopting), otherwise creates one, then polls to Ready and on deletion either orphans or deregisters (refused with KeyInUse while any instance still uses it). Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). Deletion is handled before the credentials are resolved and resolves them only to deregister; a Delete that cannot waits finalizerDeletionGracePeriod, then orphans the key with a Warning (id 157). A transient failure of the list, the adoption read or the create is retried without a status write (id 88); fail() writes phase Error; AuraCustomerManagedKeyReady is announced when the key becomes ready (ids 136, 156). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A DELETE Aura refuses — not a conflict, not transient, not "not found" — is waited on the same way: reason DeletionRefused, announced once, asked again until finalizerDeletionGracePeriod has passed, then the finalizer is released with the kind's Orphaned Warning (operations.md id 201). A key still in use (KeyInUse) is bounded the same way, then orphaned with a Warning. Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199).

name: Reconcile AuraIPFilter
description: AuraIPFilterReconciler.Reconcile: resolves spec.instanceRefs to Aura instance IDs, adopts an existing filter by name or creates one via CreateIPFilter, then converges allow_list/filtered_entities/name/filteringDisabled drift via UpdateIPFilter, and on deletion deletes or orphans the filter. Every write of its own CR (finalizer, external-ID and probe annotations) goes through one helper that applies the change to a fresh copy and writes it as a merge patch, never an Update (operations.md id 150). Deletion is handled before the credentials are resolved and resolves them (and the organization) only to delete; a Delete that cannot waits finalizerDeletionGracePeriod, then orphans the filter with a Warning (id 157). A transient failure of the list or the create is retried without a status write (id 88); AuraIPFilterReady is announced when the filter becomes Ready (ids 136, 156). Status is written only when it changes or its lastSyncedTime is auraSyncedTimeRefresh (15 minutes) old, since a status write starts another reconcile (operations.md id 156). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A DELETE Aura refuses — not a conflict, not transient, not "not found" — is waited on the same way: reason DeletionRefused, announced once, asked again until finalizerDeletionGracePeriod has passed, then the finalizer is released with the kind's Orphaned Warning (operations.md id 201). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199).

name: Reconcile Neo4jPlugin
description: Main reconcile loop: validates the spec, resolves clusterRef, refuses to install when another CR in the namespace already owns the same clusterRef and plugin name (an enabled CR wins over a disabled one, then the older by creationTimestamp, then the lower UID; only an enabled CR is held back, Failed with one PluginDuplicate, and a disabled one goes to sf-plugin-disable; operations.md id 195), then merges the plugin into the target's env/init-containers. On reaching Ready it records status.installedVersion (the spec.version it installed) and status.installationTime (set once per installed version, not touched by later reconciles or same-version Ready/Installing cycles); a plugin already Ready before those fields existed is backfilled on its next reconcile. On a standalone, the plugin's security and startup-only settings stay out of the env (the standalone controller merges them into neo4j.conf with the user's spec.config), and env copies an earlier operator wrote are removed. The controller also watches StatefulSets: a created one or a changed pod template re-queues the Ready plugins it is the target of. A settled (Ready, current generation) pass makes the plugin's edits on a copy of the live pod template; with nothing to put right it returns without Bolt, StatefulSet or status writes, whatever state the target is in; otherwise it emits PluginMissing, turns Installing and restores what is gone (a variable the plugin sets that is absent, NEO4J_PLUGINS not listing a name it needs, a standalone's leftover conf copy, a VerifiedDownload init container or volume absent by name) — never a value someone else gave one of its variables. A VerifiedDownload plugin's shared plugin-ca volume, and its init container's mount of it, that no longer follow the target's spec.trustedCASecrets are brought in line without a PluginMissing Warning (Installing, "Updating the plugin's trusted CAs: …"), since the user changed the list. The env edits and a VerifiedDownload init container and volumes are written in one StatefulSet update, the live init container replaced only when a field the plugin sets differs (the API server defaults the rest). A write to the StatefulSet restarts every server, so while the target is not Ready with every server available (a cluster Degraded, or forming, rolling or upgrading; a standalone not Ready) or has not rolled out its latest spec (status.observedGeneration behind its generation, or its StatefulSet still rolling: observedGeneration, currentRevision vs updateRevision, updated and ready replicas) a pass whose edits would change it is Waiting instead, requeued after RequeueAfter, announced once (PluginInstallDeferred, worded as a trusted-CA update when that is all it writes, or PluginMissing for a Ready plugin that lost something); a pass with nothing to write is not held, nor is a write that repairs the plugin's own failing init container (sf-plugin-self-repair). After its write the plugin stays Installing until the StatefulSet reports the template rolled out to every pod (the pass that writes compares against the generation its write created, since the cached StatefulSet may predate the write), naming any pod its init container keeps from starting, and only then turns Ready, with one PluginInstalled event from the status write that makes it Ready. There is no configuration step: every setting reaches the servers at their start (dbms.setConfigValue, which takes only dynamic settings and only on the server it runs on, is no longer called), and the Bolt functional check runs only on a pass about to write the StatefulSet, never on one waiting for its own restart. A plugin with spec.enabled false goes to sf-plugin-disable; a Managed plugin whose NEO4J_PLUGINS names the target's image does not install goes to sf-plugin-refuse-unknown-name; every pass of an enabled plugin judges whether the target's allowlist hides its procedures (sf-plugin-hidden-procedures). An install pass with nothing to change does not write the StatefulSet, and a change to a variable the cluster renders from its own spec (neo4j.com/cluster-controller-env-vars), or a NEO4J_PLUGINS that is not a JSON list, is refused as Failed rather than fought over (sf-plugin-refuse-install). Every write also records the variables the plugin sets and removes those it recorded and no longer sets (sf-plugin-env-ownership); a settled pass with nothing to put right writes only a missing record, as a metadata patch. A StatefulSet conflict or an unreachable server mid-install keeps the plugin Installing and requeues without a Warning; a real failure is Failed with one PluginInstallFailed Warning and retried every RequeueAfter. Installing is announced only where an install starts, not by a pass continuing one. While its roll is pending the message also names pods whose neo4j container keeps exiting. A target whose StatefulSet does not exist is waited for quietly, not read as drift, and a target that does not exist yet is waited for in phase Pending with one ClusterNotFound Warning (sf-plugin-await-statefulset). On deletion the finalizer takes off the target everything the plugin wrote in one write (sf-plugin-env-ownership); on a standalone whose pod keeps failing on the plugin it then waits, rechecking every five seconds and for at most five minutes from the deletion, until replaceStuckPods has deleted that pod (uninstallWaitsForStuckPod), since an OrderedReady StatefulSet does not replace a pod that is not Ready and nothing would once the finalizer is gone. The finalizer is added and released as a merge patch of metadata.finalizers, never an Update, which sent the whole object back as the Go types encode it and turned spec.enabled: false into true (operations.md id 150). Its finalizer is released by removeFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the finalizer at its index and removes it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a status write since the copy was read is no Conflict, another writer's finalizer is kept, and an object already gone is success (operations.md id 189). A Managed fleet-management plugin on an image with Fleet Manager built in (2026.03+) installs nothing and is Ready (reconcileBuiltIn), and is not judged by the ProceduresHidden check (operations.md id 192). Its finalizer is added by addFinalizer: a JSON patch that tests the list the copy has (null when it has none) and appends to it, without the resourceVersion lock, so a copy older than the object is no Conflict and another writer's finalizer is kept (operations.md id 199). It also watches Neo4jPlugins: a CR created, deleted, given a new spec or starting its deletion wakes the other CRs with its clusterRef and spec.name (and, on an update, those of its old tuple), so a duplicate held back by a CR since deleted or disabled takes over at once; status writes wake nothing (pluginsSharingTuple, tupleOwnershipChanged; operations.md id 195). A disabled CR or one being deleted takes off the target only what it alone wrote: its removal keeps what the CR that installs the same plugin in its place installs (sf-plugin-env-ownership), so neither the hand-over nor a duplicate's deletion restarts the servers. Every refusal the user must fix — an Invalid spec, a duplicate, a name the image cannot install, an install the target's spec refuses — is logged by logRefusal from the status write that records it: at info once, at V(1) after, never as an ERROR; a real failure keeps its ERROR (operations.md id 228).

name: Wait Quietly For The Target's StatefulSet
description: statefulSetAbsent and awaitStatefulSet (internal/controller/plugin_target_absent.go): when the plugin's target exists but its StatefulSet does not — the target's controller has not created it yet, or a storage expansion deleted it and creates it again, as it was, seconds later — the pass waits with no event, no ERROR log and no status write the plugin's state does not need. A plugin Ready or Disabled at its generation keeps its status and is not requeued: the StatefulSet's creation wakes a Ready plugin, whose settled pass finds what it set in a StatefulSet created as it was and writes nothing (no PluginMissing, no PluginInstalled again), and restores with one PluginMissing only what a new StatefulSet lacks. A plugin part way through its generation (Installing, Waiting, Failed — a disabled plugin's removal in flight included) keeps its status and looks again after RequeueAfter; any other plugin is Waiting ("Waiting for StatefulSet <name> of <target> to be created"). The check runs after the disabled and refusal branches and wherever a pass reads the StatefulSet (the settled drift check, installChangesTarget, the write); the ProceduresHidden condition is left as it is. A target that does not exist at all (awaitTarget: no cluster or standalone named spec.clusterRef in the namespace, a plugin reconciled before its target) is waited for too: phase Pending ("Waiting for its target: clusterRef \"<ref>\" not found …"), one ClusterNotFound Warning from the status write that starts the wait, and a look every RequeueAfter; it used to be Failed with no requeue. Only a not-found counts (errTargetNotFound); another read error is returned and retried. Before this, each plugin read the missing StatefulSet as drift during an expansion: PluginMissing and PluginInstallFailed Warnings, two ERROR logs, Installing for the whole expansion and PluginInstalled again at its end (operations.md id 177).

name: Merge NEO4J_PLUGINS list
description: MergeNeo4jPluginList live-patches the target StatefulSet's NEO4J_PLUGINS env var to add this plugin without wholesale-replacing the list, so it never clobbers a value another Neo4jPlugin/Aura Fleet controller wrote; RemoveFromNeo4jPluginList is its inverse, used by the uninstall (sf-plugin-env-ownership) for the plugin's names that no other plugin of the target installs.

name: Follow The Target's Trusted CAs
description: setPluginCAVolume keeps the plugin-ca volume that every VerifiedDownload init container of a target shares in line with the target's spec.trustedCASecrets (the plugin controller is its only writer): added when the list is not empty, replaced when it projects other Secrets, keys or paths than the list (order ignored; API-server defaults and optional flags are not compared, so an unchanged list writes nothing), removed when the list is empty and no container mounts it any more. The init script trusts the init image's default CA bundle plus the custom CAs ($CURL_CA_BUNDLE if it names a file, else the first of /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt, /etc/ssl/cert.pem, /cacert.pem; custom CAs only, with a WARNING, when the image has none), so a public download URL keeps working with a custom CA listed. Each projection is optional, and the init script falls back to the default CAs when /etc/plugin-ca holds no certificate, so a removed CA's Secret deleted before the plugin's write cannot keep a restarting server from starting; the JAR's checksum still vouches for it.

name: Repair The Plugin's Own Failing Init Container
description: selfRepair lets a plugin's write through to a target that is not Ready with every server available when it changes what keeps the target so, and nothing else: the write changes a VerifiedDownload plugin's init container or a volume it mounts, or the env the plugin gives the neo4j container; every server pod that is not Ready is failing in it — in that init container (exited non-zero and not succeeded since), or in its neo4j container (exited non-zero and not running again) while running a variable the write changes — and no pod is missing or terminating; those pods are the highest ordinals at or above the partition, which the StatefulSet's rolling update replaces first; and on a cluster Neo4j's last diagnostics report no other server unavailable. The pass skips the Bolt functional check, writes, and announces one Warning from its status write: PluginInitContainerFailing for the init container, PluginSettingsFailing for the settings. replaceStuckPods then deletes a standalone's pod stuck on an older revision once its OrderedReady StatefulSet has seen the new template — failing in that init container, or, while the plugin is not settled, crash-looping in neo4j with env the template changes outside what the standalone renders — since such a StatefulSet does not replace a pod that is not Ready (knowledge operations.md ids 152, 155). It reports whether it is still waiting for the StatefulSet to see the template, which a deleted plugin's finalizer waits on (uninstallWaitsForStuckPod: every five seconds, at most five minutes from the deletion); a deleted or disabled plugin is never settled, so its stuck pod is replaced too. It judges the plugin's next write (desiredTarget): its install edits, or for a disabled plugin its removal. On a cluster the StatefulSet's rolling update replaces the failing pods itself, except with MaxUnavailableStatefulSet on (Kubernetes 1.35.0–1.35.3), where the cluster controller deletes them (Replace Server Pods That Cannot Start, operations.md id 204).

name: Record And Remove The Plugin's Env Vars
description: applyPlugin makes the plugin's edits on a copy of its target's StatefulSet and records, under the StatefulSet annotation neo4j.com/plugin-env-vars.<plugin CR name>, the variables it sets as a whole on the neo4j container (one per spec.config key in the env; on a cluster a non-list security setting; never a shared procedure or extension list). Each write removes the variables the record lists and the plugin no longer sets — a key removed from spec.config — in the same StatefulSet update, except one the target renders itself (its own env record), one another plugin records, or one another plugin of the target sets. A plugin without a record (installed by an earlier operator) records what it sets on its first pass, as a metadata patch that restarts nothing, and removes nothing. removePluginFromTarget is the uninstall: in one write it takes off the target the plugin's recorded and current variables, its tokens in the procedure lists that no other plugin of the target needs, in Managed mode its NEO4J_PLUGINS names (mapped, e.g. gds as graph-data-science, and its dependencies) that no other Managed plugin of the target installs and not fleet-management while the target's spec.auraFleetManagement installs it, its VerifiedDownload init container and volumes, and its record; never what the target renders itself (knowledge operations.md id 155). It records its NEO4J_PLUGINS names the same way (neo4j.com/plugin-entries.<plugin>: in Managed mode its own and its dependencies'), and a write takes out those it no longer adds — a dropped dependency, every name after a switch away from Managed mode — less those another enabled Managed plugin adds and fleet-management while the target installs it. On a cluster, every write adds the plugin's own tokens to each shared procedure and extension list (automatic settings, spec.security, and list keys of spec.config) and keeps a token already there only while it or another enabled plugin of the target asks for it, keeping a value whose tokens are the same; it never adds another plugin's tokens — those arrive with that plugin's own write — and the uninstall adds nothing (operations.md id 173). The variables hold only the plugins' tokens: each server's startup script joins them with the cluster's own entries from neo4j.conf (sf-reconcile-cluster-configmap, operations.md id 179). A disabled plugin is left out of what is kept for others. A duplicate (same spec.name) is left out too, except the one that installs the plugin in place of a CR that is disabled or being deleted (pluginSuccessor): that CR's removal keeps what the successor installs, including a VerifiedDownload successor's init container and volumes (operations.md id 195). The fleet-management plugin asks for no allowlist entry on a cluster (the servers add it to an allowlist set elsewhere); a variable holding its old entry fleetManagement.* alone is taken off by its settled pass with one write (operations.md id 192).

name: Reconcile CCDR Proxy
description: Creates/updates the CCDR proxy's ConfigMap/Deployment/Service (or tears them down when disabled), then publishes status.crossClusterReplication.{ready,addresses,loadBalancerHostname} from the proxy Service's LoadBalancer ingress before the server ConfigMap is rendered.

name: Create Replica Database From Network
description: Calls CreateReplicaDatabaseFromNetwork with the upstream database name and an address list — either source.addresses directly, or resolved by sf-resolve-upstream-cluster-ref from source.upstreamClusterRef — when the target database does not yet exist (source.mode: network).

name: Resolve Upstream Cluster Ref
description: When source.upstreamClusterRef is set, reads the named Neo4jEnterpriseCluster's status.internalAddresses via a live Get and returns it as the network-mode address list; a missing or not-yet-ready upstream is reported Pending and retried rather than failed, since the upstream may simply not have reconciled yet.

name: Resolve Upstream Backup Ref
description: When source.upstreamBackupRef is set, reads the named Neo4jBackup CR's status.replicationPullURI via a live Get and returns it as the backup-mode pullURI; a missing Neo4jBackup or one that hasn't run its first backup yet is reported Pending and retried rather than failed.

name: CLI Validate
description: Runs the operator's own validators (internal/validation) over manifest files before they are applied, offline for the 21 validators that never touch the client and connected for the cross-reference ones. A Neo4jEnterpriseCluster runs the same ApplyDefaults and ValidateWithWarnings the operator runs on every pass, the defaults applied only to the copy it validates (a tls block without a mode is held to the cert-manager rules, as the API server stores it, and an authorization provider list is judged as written; operations.md id 150); a Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone runs the operator's StandaloneValidator.Validate (no defaults of the operator's own). Before any kind's validator runs, every default its CRD declares is applied to the document, as the API server stores it (withSchemaDefaults over the CRDs embedded from config/crd/bases, with the API server's structural defaulting; operations.md id 150): a standalone's tls: {} is judged as cert-manager and needs an issuerRef, a bool the CRD defaults to true reads true. For both, offline it drops any status in the manifest and its summary says the image-tag rule needs --connect; with --connect it copies in the live deployment's status, so a downgrade below the version it runs is refused (status.version, and for a tag without a patch status.runningVersion and status.upgradeStatus.resolvedTargetVersion, operations.md id 153), and one it cannot read is a warning. Each validator reports every error it finds, Neo4jShardedDatabase's included: its errors keep their own field paths, a clusterRef that names no cluster yet is Pending (as the operator waits for it), and a cluster it cannot read is a warning that the rules needing it were not checked (operations.md ids 144, 145). Distinguishes errors, warnings and Pending, prints the ruleset version it carries, and warns on skew against the operator running in the cluster. It also reports every key a kind has no field for, with its full path, by walking the document against the type's json tags, descending into lists of objects and reporting the item index (spec.topology.serverRoles[0].modeContraint) — open maps (spec.config, driverSettings), metadata and status are skipped, since their keys are data rather than field names. With --connect a Neo4jBackup's spec.shardedDatabase is resolved through ResolveBackupShardedDatabase, the function the backup controller's sharded preflight calls: a name that is no Neo4jShardedDatabase CR (naming the CR when it is that CR's logical name) or a CR on another cluster is an error, as the operator fails the backup for it (operations.md id 116). A Neo4jPlugin is held to the names the Neo4j entrypoint installs (operations.md id 170): with --connect its target is resolved as the plugin controller resolves it (PluginTargetImageTag: cluster first, then standalone) and a Managed plugin's NEO4J_PLUGINS name the target's image does not list is the operator's own error (ManagedPluginImageErrors); with no target, or one it cannot read, it says so and applies the offline rule. Offline it warns about a name no supported release installs and about n10s, which runs in Managed mode on 5.26.0–5.26.21 only (ManagedPluginNameWarnings), and its summary says the image check needs --connect; the compatibility-matrix warning is left out for a Managed name no supported image installs, which printed a second warning for graphql (managedNameUnknownToEveryImage). Connected, a deployment that does not exist yet is pending on every kind that names one (the five validators' TargetPending, the sharded database's Pending, and deploymentRefFindings for the alias, composite, replica, backup instanceRef and plugin), never an error (id 182). A cluster's or standalone's spec.storage.className is compared with the data volumes it has, found as the operator's storage pass finds them, and gives the operator's advisory warning before the apply (id 102). The version-skew warning compares with the operator that runs: a Deployment with available replicas, of several on different releases the one whose pod holds its leader-election Lease, and says it cannot tell otherwise (id 188). A Managed fleet-management plugin gets a warning: connected, when its target's image has Fleet Manager built in (ManagedPluginBuiltInWarnings); offline, that it installs nothing on 2026.03 and later (id 192).

name: CLI Preflight
description: Checks the cluster-side preconditions a manifest depends on and that no manifest-level check can see: the StorageClass exists and allows volume expansion, a Ready node can fit the memory request, imagePullSecrets exist, and a backup's credentials Secret carries every key the Job mounts or its ServiceAccount carries a cloud-identity annotation; a PVC-backed backup's named claim must exist, except that an absent claim is reported as waiting rather than failed when spec.storage.pvc.size is set, because the operator provisions it in that case, and a claim that cannot be read is a warning rather than a pass or a failure. It also checks the cloud substrate: the provider is detected from a node's spec.providerID, and a CCDR proxy asking for a private load balancer is reported as a problem when the detected provider reads none of the internal-LB annotations the operator emits, or when the Service was already assigned a public address; the cluster default StorageClass is resolved and expansion-checked when spec.storage.className is empty; a hard zone constraint is checked against the zones that exist; and a spec.securityContext override is checked against the namespace's pod-security enforce level, since the override replaces the operator's hardened default rather than merging with it. Each manifest is checked in its own metadata.namespace, as kubectl apply would place it; -n (or the kubeconfig namespace) applies only to manifests that omit one. Checks shape, never reachability: it contacts no bucket, registry or endpoint and runs no probe pod. For a backup-mode Neo4jReplicaDatabase reading s3://, it checks the same region sources as the operator (spec.env, spec.extraEnvFrom, the live container's env and envFrom); a source it cannot read is a warning, not a problem. The largest Ready node's allocatable memory is printed in the largest binary unit it reaches, rounded down to one decimal (62.2Gi), not as the node reports it in Ki.

name: CLI Status
description: Lists every Neo4j resource in a namespace with phase, readiness and age, taking the kind list from the registered scheme so a new CRD appears without code changes. An unrecognised phase is not treated as a problem, and Pending messages are shown as guidance rather than failure. With --problems it lists the phases Failed, Error, Invalid, ValidationFailed (a Neo4jDatabase's name for Invalid), Degraded and Unknown, decided from the phase alone (status.ready is omitempty and never stores false); the message block under the table covers only the rows shown. A Neo4jEnterpriseCluster whose status.upgradeStatus.phase is Failed or Paused is a problem under --problems although its phase stays Ready: the PHASE column reads 'Ready (upgrade Failed)' and the note adds the upgrade's last error (#565; operations.md id 149).

name: CLI Diagnose
description: Explains why a resource is unhealthy at the Kubernetes level: unschedulable pods, OOMKills (kubelet reason or exit code 137) and non-zero exits, read from both the previous and the current container state so a Job pod under RestartPolicyNever (which never restarts, leaving its last state empty) is reported with the plain log command and, for a backup, the Neo4jBackup's own spec.options.resources, image-pull and crash-loop states (a crash-looping container is not reported twice), unbound PVCs, failed backup Jobs (judged by the Job's Failed and Complete conditions rather than the cumulative status.failed attempt count, so a backup that retried and then completed is not an error; the leftover failed pods of a Job that did not fail are softened to warning or waiting findings), warning events that still describe the resource's current state (seen at or after its Ready condition last changed, or an advisory in controller.AdvisoryWarningReasons seen within the 30-minute refresh; earlier ones are counted in one line, not marked, and change neither --quiet nor the exit code; operations.md id 168), and custom resources the operator has never written status to. Finds workloads through the operator's exported selectors and anchors rules to Kubernetes API constants where they exist. Exits 1 when a problem is found. A cluster or standalone with neither StatefulSet nor pods is told to check the operator only when the operator has written no status; with a status (a refused spec, a missing StorageClass) the hint (noWorkloadAction) points at the status message, or the conditions and events, and at explain (operations.md id 154). A cluster whose upgrade stopped (Failed or Paused) gets a problem line 'upgrade to <target> is <phase>' with its last error and what to do, since the cluster's phase stays Ready (#565; operations.md id 149).

name: CLI Explain
description: Decodes a status condition, phase or condition REASON into what it means and what to do, keyed off the operator's exported condition constants so a rename breaks the build rather than leaving the explanation stale. A live resource's conditions are printed with their reason, explained after the condition's general guidance since the reason is the more specific signal; only reasons that are not guessable from the string itself get an entry. Negative-polarity conditions (ClusterNotReady, Degraded, ServersPendingDrain, UserNotFound, PendingDependencies, AuthRuleVersionTooOld) are marked healthy when False, and their problem guidance is shown only when True. Every phase of the shared vocabulary (api/v1beta1 AllPhases) has guidance, Neo4jAuthRule's PendingDependencies included (it was a controller literal, so explain called it newer than the CLI; operations.md id 154). The Unknown phase is explained as one only operators up to v1.21 write (a Neo4jDatabase whose target had no seed credentials Secret), which a current operator replaces on its next pass (operations.md id 190). Reports unrecognised terms as unrecognised, naming its own version.

name: CLI Connect and Cypher
description: Resolves how to reach a deployment — admin Secret, pod and container, and the Bolt scheme from the deployment kind and spec.tls (neo4j/neo4j+s routing for a cluster, bolt/bolt+s for a standalone) — and either prints the connection details or hands over an interactive cypher-shell session via kubectl exec. The printed details give the same in-cluster address the session dials; for a port-forward under TLS they say that the certificate never names localhost and offer the +ssc variant for local testing only. The password is referenced by env var inside the pod and never passes through this process or the audit log.

name: CLI Export Replica Database
description: Authors a Neo4jReplicaDatabase manifest for a downstream on a DIFFERENT Kubernetes cluster, filling source.pullURI from an upstream Neo4jBackup's status.replicationPullURI or source.addresses from an upstream cluster's cross-cluster replication status. Same-cluster users are pointed back at upstreamBackupRef and upstreamClusterRef, which the operator resolves live. Output is validated with the operator's own ReplicaValidator before it is printed.

name: CLI Support Bundle
description: Collects custom resources, workloads, events and pod logs into one redacted archive. Secret values, last-applied-configuration annotations and sensitive-looking literal environment variables are never included; valueFrom references are kept because they explain failures and hold no secret. Every redaction is enumerated in REDACTIONS.txt. Collection is best-effort: every read that fails (a CR-kind, events, pods, secrets-listing, container-log or operator read) is skipped without aborting and listed, as the read plus its error text only, in errors.txt, and the command prints how many reads failed.

name: Normalise Role Privileges
description: normaliseDesired() maps each spec.privileges statement to the rows Neo4j actually stores for it (lists expanded, plurals singularised, default segments filled, verbs renamed, database names lower-cased, aliases resolved), using a probe of the statement on a throwaway role, cached per target UID, image and the targets of the aliases the role's statements name (every alias for a role with a statement whose targets cannot be read) with a 1h TTL; with the alias layout unreadable it probes without the cache. Statements naming a missing database, or whose probe fails, fall back to textual canonicalisation (internal/controller/neo4jrole_normalise.go).

name: Probe privilege rendering
description: ProbePrivilegeRendering creates a throwaway operator_privilege_probe_<random> role, grants one privilege statement to it, reads SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES AS COMMANDS back and drops the role, all in one system-database session so the read is causally after the grant (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Learn Role Privileges
description: Learn mode (--privilege-normalisation=learn, the default; the probe is opt-in): reconcileLearned()/learnDesired() learn each spec statement's stored rows from the operator's own grant (before/after diff), persist them in status.privilegeRenderings BEFORE any revoke, never revoke status.unattributedPrivileges, and re-learn on scope change, a vanished unattributed row, or revocation of a removed statement's rows. Fails loudly when the installed CRD prunes these status fields (internal/controller/neo4jrole_learn.go). The rendering scope (roleRenderingScope) covers the target UID, its image and only the aliases the role's statements name, so an alias change elsewhere on the cluster re-learns nothing; statements on *, HOME, DEFAULT and DBMS name no alias, and only a role with a statement whose targets cannot be read stays on every alias. Names are read as Neo4j lists them: a constituent by its qualified name however its parts are quoted, a doubled backtick as one literal backtick. A pass that cannot list databases or aliases keeps the learned scope instead of re-learning. Only grants that created a row count toward PrivilegesApplied, so a re-learn's no-op grants are not reported (knowledge operations.md ids 136, 142). A statement whose grant added no row is attributed to the stored row its own text is, with only the database and graph names compared ignoring case (storedFormRows, FoldPrivilegeDatabaseNames), so `ACCESS ON DATABASE TOPODB` next to `ON DATABASES topodb, other` is no longer ambiguous and out-of-band rows stay revocable (operations.md ids 20, 146). A statement already held ambiguous whose stored row is now found is settled from it without a grant, so a role learned before the fix settles on the first pass after the upgrade. A row another session grants between the two reads of one learning grant is learned as that statement's — a known limit; removing it by hand re-learns the statement without it.

name: Grant and read privileges
description: GrantAndReadPrivileges runs SHOW ROLE PRIVILEGES, one GRANT/DENY, and SHOW again in a single system-database session, returning the before/after rows so learn mode can attribute exactly the rows the statement created; transient 25N11 conflicts retry the whole sequence (internal/neo4j/users.go).

name: Reconcile Server Shortfall
description: Sets the status of a cluster that is not fully formed. Feeds the formation result, the ClusterFormed memory, whether a template rollout is in flight and the Degraded condition's lastTransitionTime to the shortfall assessment, then writes Ready (Degraded condition True) within the grace period, Degraded past it, or Forming — for first formation, rollouts, scale-ups, split-brain or the loss of a majority (#444). When Neo4j could not be queried it also feeds the number of Ready server pods and when the connection-failure streak began; an Unmeasured verdict writes nothing. ClusterDegraded and ClusterQuorumLost are deduplicated in memory, since the informer cache can return the previous phase. Its messages for a formed cluster short of a server (within the grace, Degraded, a lost majority) say what Neo4j reports and, while Neo4j still lists every server available, which server pods Kubernetes does not report ready (terminating, not ready, missing) — never the formation or rollout check's detail, which is kept for a cluster that is Forming (#553). ClusterFormationStarted is announced from what the write entering Forming replaced, as the API server held it (knowledge operations.md ids 105, 136). A formed cluster whose majority is back, short of a server within the grace, is written Ready from Forming: that write announces ClusterReady, and the pass that finds every server back later announces nothing more (#606; operations.md id 136). It reads which of the expected server pods Kubernetes does not report ready before the assessment, and a NoneShort verdict writes nothing: the Degraded condition says True only while a server, or a server pod, is short, and its message names it (#608; operations.md id 225).

name: Assess Server Shortfall
description: Pure decision for a formed cluster short of servers: a server that stays Enabled in SHOW SERVERS but is not Available is lost, one never Enabled is joining. With more than half the expected servers available the verdict is WithinGrace, then Degraded once the shortfall outlasts the grace period; half or fewer is QuorumLost; never formed, a rollout, a split-brain, Neo4j unreachable or fewer Enabled servers than expected is Forming — except that a formed cluster Neo4j cannot be asked about, while Kubernetes reports a majority of its server pods Ready and the connection-failure streak is younger than the grace period, is Unmeasured, and nothing is written. A member is a server Enabled or Cordoned (a cordoned server that is down is lost, not joining; operations.md id 224). When every expected server is an available member and Kubernetes reports each of their pods ready, nothing is short: the verdict is NoneShort and nothing is written. It used to write Degraded=True "3 of 3 servers available" for about ten seconds after every scale-down drain (#608; operations.md id 225).

name: Resolve Backup Sharded Database
description: ResolveBackupShardedDatabase() (internal/validation/backup_sharded_ref.go) reads the Neo4jShardedDatabase a ShardedDatabase-scope Neo4jBackup names in spec.shardedDatabase: by the CR's metadata.name in the backup's namespace, never by the logical spec.name, and on the backup's spec.instanceRef. It returns a refusal at spec.shardedDatabase for a name that is no such CR (naming the CR whose spec.name matches it, ignoring case) or a CR on another cluster, and an error for any other read failure. The backup controller's sharded preflight and kubectl neo4j validate --connect both call it, so the CLI refuses what the operator fails (operations.md id 116).

name: Validate Neo4jShardedDatabase spec
description: ShardedDatabaseValidator.Validate runs every rule on the spec (name, clusterRef present, property shard count, seed options, replaceExisting gates, topology, Cypher 25) whatever happens to the cluster read, then the rules that need the referenced Neo4jEnterpriseCluster (property sharding enabled, room for the shards) when it can be read. A cluster that does not exist yet is Pending, never an error, so the reconciler reaches its documented wait (phase Pending, ClusterNotFound); any other read failure is ClusterReadErr. ValidateShardedDatabase, the reconciler's entry point, returns the field errors and a read failure as one error. Before #532 a failed read returned alone, dropping the spec errors, and a missing cluster made the database Failed (internal/validation/shardeddatabase_validator.go; operations.md id 145).

name: Warn On An Unapplied StorageClass
description: recordStorageClassChange, on every storage pass of a cluster and a standalone: lists the data PVCs and, while spec.storage.className names a StorageClass some of them do not use, raises an advisory ValidationWarning naming each volume and its class (validation.StorageClassChangeWarning). A volume keeps the class it was created with and the StatefulSet's claim template cannot change, so an edit of className reaches no existing volume. An empty className (the cluster default) and a deployment without volumes say nothing; the warning is recorded in its own advisoryWarnings scope, apart from the validator's ValidationWarning set (internal/controller/storage_class_change.go; operations.md id 102). The volumes are found by ClusterDataVolumeClasses / StandaloneDataVolumeClasses, which `kubectl neo4j validate --connect` calls too.

name: Refuse Upgrade Start
description: Records an upgrade that a check refused before anything was written to the server StatefulSet — the version rule (the whole tag rule against status, ValidateTagAgainstRunning) or the pre-upgrade check (health, consensus, a leader, and the target not below the highest version SHOW SERVERS reports): Paused with autoPauseOnFailure, Failed otherwise, with the cause in lastError. The UpgradeFailed or UpgradePaused Warning and the failure metric follow only a write that changed the record's phase, target or error. The cluster stays Ready and its status.message names the stopped upgrade; a Failed one is tried again after one minute, with the normal pass running in between. It used to fail the cluster too, flipping it between Failed and Ready with an UpgradeFailed and a ClusterReady every cycle (#538, #531; operations.md id 149).

name: Replace Servers That Cannot Start On The Target
description: Takes up a Paused or Failed upgrade towards a new spec.image.tag although the cluster is short of servers, when the servers down are exactly the ones it restarted, each unable to start on its image (an image pull that fails, a container that keeps exiting, a failing init container), the highest ordinals at or above the partition, every server below them up, and Neo4j's last view names no other server unavailable. It skips the every-replica-ready gate and the pre-upgrade health check, and Staging freezes at the lowest of those servers so the StatefulSet replaces them on the new template first; the walk goes on from there through its gates. Changing the tag did nothing before, towards any tag (#538; operations.md id 162). It compares the tag with the image the down servers run, not with the template; a Paused upgrade whose tag the user has not changed waits. With every server frozen (the partition at the replica count) it also takes up servers down on another image than every server that is up — recreated from a revision the walk had not put them on — which left the cluster stuck before (#562 re-walk; operations.md id 162). Staging judges those servers from the pods as the API server has them (operations.md id 203), and where the StatefulSet does not replace them itself (Kubernetes 1.35.0–1.35.3) the walk deletes them (operations.md id 204).

name: Hold Topology During Upgrade
description: Keeps the server count where it is while an upgrade is in flight or a Paused or Failed one keeps a partition: Staging writes the StatefulSet's own replica count, and the normal pass of a held upgrade works on that count in memory, so no server is added on the target, no drain runs mid-upgrade, and the formation check expects the servers there are. The TopologyChangeDeferred condition names both counts and the upgrade; the change is applied once the upgrade completes. Staging used to apply spec.topology.servers, removing servers with no drain on a scale-down in the same apply as an image change (#538; operations.md id 163).

name: Take A Disabled Plugin Off Its Target
description: reconcileDisabled: for a Neo4jPlugin with spec.enabled false, the uninstall write of a deleted plugin (withoutPlugin: its NEO4J_PLUGINS names, variables, list tokens, VerifiedDownload init container and volumes, records) in one StatefulSet update, while the CR stays. The write waits like an install for a target that is Ready with every server available and rolled out (Waiting, one PluginInstallDeferred, "removing the disabled plugin restarts every server"), except when every down server keeps failing in what the plugin set (sf-plugin-self-repair judges the removal). Installing while the removal rolls out, then Disabled with one PluginDisabled event; a plugin with nothing on its target is Disabled at once. A target whose StatefulSet does not exist is waited for (sf-plugin-await-statefulset): a Disabled plugin stays Disabled, a removal in flight stays Installing. spec.enabled true installs it again (knowledge operations.md id 160). A disabled CR is never held back as a duplicate: when an enabled Neo4jPlugin installs the same spec.name on the target, the removal keeps what that CR installs (its NEO4J_PLUGINS names, variables, list tokens, and a VerifiedDownload init container and volumes of the same names), and the Disabled message names it ("Neo4jPlugin "<name>" installs "<plugin>" on <target> in its place"; operations.md id 195). The status write that makes the plugin Disabled clears status.installedVersion and status.installationTime; enabled again, its next Ready records a new installation (operations.md id 196).

name: Refuse A Plugin Name The Target's Image Cannot Install
description: reconcileRefused, with ManagedPluginImageErrors (internal/validation/plugin_entrypoint.go): the Neo4j Docker entrypoint exits on a NEO4J_PLUGINS name its image's /startup/neo4j-plugins.json does not list, so a Managed, enabled Neo4jPlugin whose name or dependency name (after the aliases gds and neosemantics) the list of its target's spec.image.tag lacks is refused. The lists are one table per release, read from neo4j/docker-neo4j at every release tag: apoc, apoc-extended, bloom, genai and graph-data-science everywhere; n10s on 5.26 and CalVer before 2025.05.0; fleet-management from 5.26.11 and 2025.08.0; graphql nowhere. A tag without a patch is its line's newest patch, a CalVer newer than the table its newest list. A listed name whose JAR the release does not run is refused too (entrypointBrokenPlugins, "not a plugin the neo4j:<tag> image can run in installMode Managed: <why>; <instead>"): n10s from 5.26.22, where the neosemantics 5.26.0 JAR the entrypoint downloads for every 5.26.x bundles jackson-annotations 2.18.0 and Neo4j's Jackson 2.21+ stops the server at startup (NoSuchMethodError JsonProperty.isRequired()), and n10s on CalVer 2025.01–2025.04, for which neosemantics' versions.json names no JAR; n10s on 5.26.0–5.26.21 is installed. The plugin is Failed with the field error ("spec.name: Invalid value: ...: not a plugin the neo4j:<tag> image can install: ...; install its JAR with installMode: VerifiedDownload (source.url + source.checksum) instead") and one PluginUnknownToImage Warning, announced from the status write that moves it into the refusal; nothing is written to the target, and it is looked at again every RequeueAfter. What an earlier write left there (its recorded NEO4J_PLUGINS names and, with no record, its own and its dependencies' mapped names, its variables, list tokens and records) comes off in the disabled plugin's single write, gated like it: at once with one PluginSettingsFailing Warning when every down server keeps failing on it, otherwise once the target is Ready with every server available. A refused plugin is left out of otherPlugins, a standalone's neo4j.conf union and the allowlist check. VerifiedDownload and PreBaked plugins are never refused (operations.md id 170; #563). Its log line follows the Warning: at info when the refusal is announced, at V(1) on the passes and steps after, never an ERROR (reportRefused; operations.md id 228).

name: Report Procedures The Allowlist Hides
description: reportHiddenProcedures: on every pass of an enabled plugin, settled ones included, reads the dbms.security.procedures.allowlist the target's servers will start with (on a cluster resources.ServerProcedureList: the union of its neo4j.conf's list, fleetManagement.* when fleet-management is installed and the list is set, and the neo4j container's NEO4J_dbms_security_procedures_allowlist, which its startup script joins, operations.md ids 179, 192; on a standalone that variable when someone else set it, which replaces neo4j.conf's, else the neo4j.conf's — a list variable of its own spec.env is in the conf, id 193). The neo4j.conf is the one the target's controller renders for its spec now (BuildConfigMapForEnterprise; desiredStandaloneConfigMap with the live ConfigMap's foreign keys merged back), not the ConfigMap as it is, so a ConfigMap an earlier operator wrote, or one not yet rewritten for a spec change, raises no transient Warning, and a new list that hides the plugin is reported at once (operations.md id 194) and, for a plugin whose procedure namespaces the operator knows (apoc., gds., bloom., genai./ai., n10s., fleetManagement.), sets the condition ProceduresHidden (True, reason NotInAllowlist) when no entry can match them, naming the list, the plugins that set it and, when its own spec.config does, the target's own configuration, with one PluginProceduresHidden Warning when the condition appears or changes; removes it silently otherwise, and on a plugin that is not on its target (disabled, or refused by its image, operations.md id 170). While the target's StatefulSet does not exist the condition is left as it is (operations.md id 177). The list is not widened (knowledge operations.md id 161).

name: Record What An Upgrade's Servers Started On
description: Lists the cluster's server pods and records status.upgradeStatus.startedTargetVersion = targetVersion once one pod's neo4j container runs the target tag and has started on it: running, terminated, terminated before, or restarted (a crash loop may have touched the store). A container waiting on an image pull that fails or a container that could not be created has not. Written only when it changes; a failed read or write is retried on the next pass. With an earlier release's CRDs the API server drops the field: the write is resent each pass, changes nothing, and is logged at V(1), not at info. Called on every Rolling pass, before a retarget re-stages, before startRollingUpgrade takes a held upgrade up, and on the normal passes that hold one. The version rule holds spec.image.tag to it, where it read progress, which says a server was released onto the target, not that it ran it: an upgrade paused on an unpublished tag could not be pointed at an earlier fixed one and the cluster went Failed (#562 walk; operations.md id 149).

name: Drop An Abandoned Upgrade Record
description: Sets status.upgradeStatus to nil for a Paused or Failed upgrade that no server started on, that resolved no version, whose target spec.image.tag no longer names, and whose target the server StatefulSet's template does not carry (a check refused it before Staging, or the tag moved back before it went on), re-read inside RetryOnConflict. Nothing would take it up, and the cluster's message said it failed and would be taken up again for as long as it stayed (#562 walk). A record with no target, or one whose template carries its target, is left (operations.md id 149).

name: Recreate StatefulSet As It Was
description: Creates the StatefulSet a storage expansion orphan-deleted with the deleted one's pod template, replica count, update strategy (a held upgrade's partition) and annotations (the ownership records of the cluster and the plugins), and the new volume claim templates, so the revision is the same and no pod restarts; the next pass applies the spec as usual. The deleted StatefulSet is kept in memory (a sync.Map, per deployment UID) from the delete to the create; after an operator restart the template is read uncached from the ControllerRevision the highest-ordinal orphaned pod runs (RBAC get on controllerrevisions), with the partition from the upgrade record. Never from a pod's spec, which admission has changed. Cluster and standalone. It used to create it from the deployment's own template, without NEO4J_PLUGINS, the plugins' variables, procedure lists, init containers and volumes: the walk lost quorum to an ungated roll and the plugins for about 17 minutes (#562 walk; operations.md id 171). It is created in the same pass as the delete, once the API server and the cache both have it no more (bounded wait, then a 1s requeue); the next pass used to read it from the cache and create it about 10s later. Under a held partition whose servers below it run another revision, it is created in two steps: first on their template, frozen at the replica count, so Kubernetes records that as the current revision (a new StatefulSet's current revision is otherwise its template); then, once the controller has recorded it, the held template and partition are written back (annotations neo4j.com/recreate-restore-partition and -revision carry the step across an operator restart). Servers below the partition then come back on the version they run if they restart; created on the held target, they came back on it, ungated (#562 re-walk). Read from a revision, the template hash is stamped when the apply of what the operator renders would leave the template as the API server stores it: both templates go through the write about to be made (the create, or the update of the live StatefulSet) as a dry run and are compared as returned, since a revision holds the defaulted and converted template and the builder none of it; compared as they were, they never matched on a real cluster and the hash stayed absent until Staging wrote the template (re-walk of 2a50fa56). A refused dry run stamps nothing; the next write of the template stamps it (operations.md id 171).

name: Validate Neo4jDatabase spec
description: DatabaseValidator.Validate: the name rules, the no-effect warnings, then the host named by spec.clusterRef (cluster, else standalone) for the rules that need it — topology against its servers, the Cypher language and seed restoreUntil against its image. A host that does not exist yet is TargetPending, never an error, and the rules of the spec alone still run (seed URI, options, conflicts; a topology held to non-negative counts); before #566 it was a spec.clusterRef error that returned at once (internal/validation/database_validator.go; operations.md id 182).

name: Stage A Retarget Without Sending A Server Back
description: When Staging writes a new target (a retarget mid-walk, or the resume of a Paused or Failed upgrade), it never puts a server that runs a newer revision than the StatefulSet's current one below the partition: it stages at the lowest such server, read from the pods uncached. Kubernetes creates a pod below the partition from the current revision — the version before the upgrade — so a server the walk had rolled onto the earlier target, recreated by a node drain or eviction, came back on the version before, a downgrade. The servers at or above that partition are moved on by the StatefulSet controller, highest first, each once the one before is Ready (Kubernetes readiness only between them); the walk's checks apply from the lowest of them down. The write waits until every server below is Ready; when every server runs the template being left, it waits for Kubernetes to record it as current and then freezes every server, so every server gets the walk's checks (operations.md id 180). During a repair with every server on the earlier target and one that cannot start on it, Kubernetes never records that target as current, so it stages at the lowest server that moved on — partition 0 when all did — a roll paced by readiness, which is a server available in the cluster (operations.md id 181); freezing at the repair partition would leave servers below it to come back on the version before if recreated (decided in round 8, operations.md id 180).

name: Replace Server Pods That Cannot Start
description: Deletes a server pod the StatefulSet's update is to replace and that cannot start: at or above the partition, below the replica count, on another revision than the status.updateRevision of a spec the StatefulSet controller has seen, not being deleted, not Ready, and failing to start (podCannotStart), read from the API server and deleted with its UID as a precondition, so that the StatefulSet creates it again from the update revision; one ServerPodReplaced event each. It runs after the normal pass's StatefulSet apply, while the cached StatefulSet shows an update that has not reached every pod with one not Ready, and on each rolling-upgrade Rolling pass with a replica not Ready. Kubernetes 1.35.0–1.35.3 run MaxUnavailableStatefulSet on, and their StatefulSet controller replaces no pod while one is unavailable — the pod that cannot start is one — so the repairs of a cluster short of a server never reached it; 1.37's controller, and the one without the gate, delete such a pod too, and one of the two deletes finds it gone. A pod below the partition, one still starting and one on the update revision are never touched (operations.md id 204).

name: Refuse A Plugin Install The Target's Spec Refuses
description: refuseInstall and pluginInstallRefusal (internal/controller/plugin_install_refusal.go): an install the user must fix in the target's spec is a status, not a controller error. Two refusals: a write that would change a variable the cluster renders from its own spec — typically NEO4J_PLUGINS in its spec.env without the plugin's name — which the cluster controller would put back, restarting the servers in turn (pluginEnvOwnedError, via ownedEnvRefusal; operations.md id 135); and a NEO4J_PLUGINS on the target that is not a JSON list of names (pluginListUnreadableError). installChangesTarget returns the first for an install, so the pass refuses before the gate that waits for a Ready target and the Bolt check that it answers; writePluginToTarget keeps its check for a record that changed in between. The plugin is Failed with "Plugin installation refused: <reason>", one PluginInstallFailed Warning and one info line from the status write that records it, V(1) on the passes after, never an ERROR or a returned error; it is looked at again every RequeueAfter, since the fix is in the target's spec and the StatefulSet watch wakes only Ready plugins. It logged ERROR "Failed to install plugin" with a stack trace on every retry, about every 27 seconds (#608, the walk of #613; operations.md id 228).
